attachments.name: Brain-To-Brain Communication: Now A Reality
attachments.description: Soldiers able to communicate silently could change the face of warfare on the ground, and perhaps the mind reading technology could prove to be more dangerous than the nuclear bomb.

attachments.name: Brain-to-brain communication: the possible role of brain electromagnetic fields (As a Potential Hypothesis)
attachments.description: Up now, the communication between brains of different humans or animals has been confirmed and confined by the sensory medium and motor facilities of body. Recently, direct brain-to-brain communication (DBBC) outside the conventional five senses has been verified between animals and humans. Nevertheless, no empirical studies or serious discussion have been performed to elucidate the mechanism behind this process. The validation of DBBC has been documented via recording similar pattern of action potentials occurring in the brain cortex of two animals. With regard to action potentials in brain neurons, the magnetic field resulting from the action potentials created in neurons is one of the tools where the brain of one animal can affect the brain of another. It has been shown that different animals, even humans, have the power to understand the magnetic field. Cryptochrome, which exists in the retina and in different regions of the brain, has been confirmed to be able to perceive magnetic fields and convert magnetic fields to action potentials. Recently, iron particles (Fe3O4) believed to be functioning as magnets have been found in various parts of the brain, and are postulated as magnetic field receptors. Newly developed supersensitive magnetic sensors made of iron magnets that can sense the brain's magnetic field have suggested the idea that these Fe3O4 particles or magnets may be capable of perceiving the brain's extremely weak magnetic field. The present study suggests that it is possible the extremely week magnetic field in one animal's brain to transmit vital and accurate information to another animal's brain.

attachments.name: Researcher controls colleague’s motions in 1st human brain-to-brain interface
attachments.description: University of Washington researchers have performed what they believe is the first noninvasive human-to-human brain interface, with one researcher able to send a brain signal via the Internet to control the hand motions of a fellow researcher.

attachments.name: Beyond Boundaries by Miguel Nicolelis
attachments.description: Imagine living in a world where people use their computers, drive their cars, and communicate with one another simply by thinking. In this stunning and inspiring work, Duke University neuroscientist Miguel Nicolelis shares his revolutionary insights into how the brain creates thought and the human sense of self—and how this might be augmented by machines, so that the entire universe will be within our reach.Beyond Boundaries draws on Nicolelis's ground-breaking research with monkeys that he taught to control the movements of a robot located halfway around the globe by using brain signals alone. Nicolelis's work with primates has uncovered a new method for capturing brain function—by recording rich neuronal symphonies rather than the activity of single neurons. His lab is now paving the way for a new treatment for Parkinson's, silk-thin exoskeletons to grant mobility to the paralyzed, and breathtaking leaps in space exploration, global communication, manufacturing, and more.Beyond Boundaries promises to reshape our concept of the technological future, to a world filled with promise and hope.

attachments.description: The last question was asked for the first time, half in jest, on May 21, 2061, at a time when humanity first stepped into the light.

attachments.description: Recently, we proposed that Brainets, i.e. networks formed by multiple animal brains, cooperating and exchanging information in real time through direct brain-to-brain interfaces, could provide the core of a new type of computing device: an organic computer.

attachments.description: SpaceX and Tesla CEO Elon Musk is backing a brain-computer interface venture called Neuralink, according to The Wall Street Journal. The company, which is still in the earliest stages of existence...

attachments.name: Computing Arm Movements with a Monkey Brainet.
attachments.description: Traditionally, brain-machine interfaces (BMIs) extract motor commands from a single brain to control the movements of artificial devices. Here, we introduce a Brainet that utilizes very-large-scale brain activity (VLSBA) from two (B2) or three (B3) nonhuman primates to engage in a common motor behaviour.

attachments.name: Monkey 'brain net' raises prospect of human brain-to-brain connection.
attachments.description: In two separate experiments, scientists have formed a network from the brains of monkeys and rats, allowing them to co-operate and learn as a “superbrain”

attachments.name: RedDevil 4 by Eric C. Leuthardt
attachments.description: Renowned neurosurgeon Dr. Hagan Maerici is on the verge of a breakthrough in artificial intelligence that could change the way we think about human consciousness.

attachments.name: Conscious Brain-to-Brain Communication in Humans Using Non-Invasive Technologies
attachments.description: Human sensory and motor systems provide the natural means for the exchange of information between individuals, and, hence, the basis for human civilization. The recent development of brain-computer interfaces (BCI) has provided an important element for the creation of brain-to-brain communication systems, and precise brain stimulation techniques are now available for the realization of non-invasive computer-brain interfaces (CBI). These technologies, BCI and CBI, can be combined to realize the vision of non-invasive, computer-mediated brain-to-brain (B2B) communication between subjects (hyperinteraction). Here we demonstrate the conscious transmission of information between human brains through the intact scalp and without intervention of motor or peripheral sensory systems. Pseudo-random binary streams encoding words were transmitted between the minds of emitter and receiver subjects separated by great distances, representing the realization of the first human brain-to-brain interface. In a series of experiments, we established internet-mediated B2B communication by combining a BCI based on voluntary motor imagery-controlled electroencephalographic (EEG) changes with a CBI inducing the conscious perception of phosphenes (light flashes) through neuronavigated, robotized transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS), with special care taken to block sensory (tactile, visual or auditory) cues. Our results provide a critical proof-of-principle demonstration for the development of conscious B2B communication technologies. More fully developed, related implementations will open new research venues in cognitive, social and clinical neuroscience and the scientific study of consciousness. We envision that hyperinteraction technologies will eventually have a profound impact on the social structure of our civilization and raise important ethical issues.

attachments.name: Brain-to-Brain Communication Based on Wireless Technologies: Actual and Future Perspectives
attachments.description: During the last few years, intensive research efforts are being done in the field of brain interfaces to extract neuro-information from the signals representing neuronal activities in the human brain. Recent development of brain-to-computer interfaces support direct communication between animals' brains, enabling direct brain-to-brain communication. Although these results are based on binary communication with relaxed requirements of latency and throughput, the fast development in neuro-science technologies indicates potential new scenarios for wireless communications between brains. In this paper we highlight technologies that are being used today to enable brain-to-brain communication and propose potential wireless communication architectures and requirements for future scenarios.

attachments.name: Scientists Discover New Brain Communication Method, Hinting At Greater Processing Power
attachments.description: The newly discovered dCaAPs offer an additional communication channel, potentially enabling more complex information processing within the brain.

attachments.name: Neuroscience – Brain Mind Institute
attachments.description: Researchers in the EPFL Brain Mind Institute (BMI) develop and deploy technology to understand brain systems across scales from theory, to molecules, cells, circuits and behavior.

description.shortText: A digital storage system that enables users to record, access, and retrieve their own memories in high fidelity. Using advanced nano-optic cameras coupled with the human eye, this technology streams recorded experiences to a secure cloud platform, allowing seamless playback and search functionalities.
description.longTextHtml:
Human Memory Digital Storage integrates nano-scale cameras with the human eye to continuously record visual experiences. These recordings are processed using AI-driven image recognition and natural language processing to tag, categorize, and store memories for future retrieval. The system automatically uploads data to a cloud service, where users can search for specific events using keywords, timestamps, or contextual cues.

The technology has the potential to redefine personal and collective memory, offering applications ranging from legal evidence collection to medical diagnostics. In legal scenarios, it could provide irrefutable proof in court cases, while in healthcare, it could assist in tracking dietary habits, allergic reactions, or early symptoms of neurodegenerative diseases. The ability to edit, organize, and externalize memory may ultimately reshape human identity and cognitive function, altering the way people interact with their own past.

Future Perspectives

Future iterations of this technology could leverage DNA-based data storage, allowing near-infinite archiving of human memory with minimal energy consumption. The integration of neural interfaces might enable users to recall memories instantly, without needing a visual interface, effectively merging external storage with brain activity.

This technology holds promise for therapeutic applications, particularly for individuals suffering from Alzheimer's or dementia. By restoring lost memories or reinforcing neural pathways, it could provide a cognitive safety net. However, such advancements also raise ethical concerns. If digital memory surpasses biological recall, people might rely more on external storage than their own minds, fundamentally changing human cognition. In a society where nothing is forgotten, the concept of privacy, relationships, and personal growth could be profoundly altered. Would the ability to delete or selectively erase digital memories become a necessity, or would forgetting become a lost function of the human mind?

attachments.name: Analysing privacy in visual lifelogging
attachments.description: The visual lifelogging activity enables a user, the lifelogger, to passively capture images from a first-person perspective and ultimately create a visual diary encoding every possible aspect of her life with unprecedented details. In recent years, it has gained popularities among different groups of users. However, the possibility of ubiquitous presence of lifelogging devices specifically in private spheres has raised serious concerns with respect to personal privacy. In this article, we have presented a thorough discussion of privacy with respect to visual lifelogging. We have re-adjusted the existing definition of lifelogging to reflect different aspects of privacy and introduced a first-ever privacy threat model identifying several threats with respect to visual lifelogging. We have also shown how the existing privacy guidelines and approaches are inadequate to mitigate the identified threats. Finally, we have outlined a set of requirements and guidelines that can be used to mitigate the identified threats while designing and developing a privacy-preserving framework for visual lifelogging.

attachments.name: Tom Gruber: How AI can enhance our memory, work and social lives
attachments.description: How smart can our machines make us? Tom Gruber, co-creator of Siri, wants to make "humanistic AI" that augments and collaborates with us instead of competing with (or replacing) us. He shares his vision for a future where AI helps us achieve superhuman performance in perception, creativity and cognitive function -- from turbocharging our design skills to helping us remember everything we've ever read and the name of everyone we've ever met. "We are in the middle of a renaissance in AI," Gruber says. "Every time a machine gets smarter, we get smarter."

attachments.description: Neo Mohsenvand records everything that happens to him, from his heartbeat to his breakfast.

attachments.description: Neurotechnologists are working to merge natural brain function with AI in hopes of augmenting human cognition & mining the mind for data.

attachments.name: Exhalation: Stories
attachments.description: Exhalation: Stories is a collection of short stories by American writer Ted Chiang. The book was initially released on May 7, 2019 by Alfred A. Knopf. This is Ted Chiang's second collection of short works, after the 2002 book Stories of Your Life and Others. Exhalation: Stories contains nine stories exploring such issues as humankind's place in the universe, the nature of humanity, bioethics, virtual reality, free will and determinism, time travel, and the uses of robotic forms of A.I.[1] Seven tales were initially published between 2005 and 2015; "Omphalos" and "Anxiety is the Dizziness of Freedom" are originals.[2][3]

attachments.name: Modulation of Human Memory by Deep Brain Stimulation of the Entorhinal-Hippocampal Circuitry - ScienceDirect
attachments.description: Neurological disorders affecting human memory present a major scientific, medical, and societal challenge. Direct or indirect deep brain stimulation (DBS) of the entorhinal-hippocampal system, the brain’s major memory hub, has been studied in people with epilepsy or Alzheimer’s disease, intending to enhance memory performance or slow memory decline. Variability in the spatiotemporal parameters of stimulation employed to date notwithstanding, it is likely that future DBS for memory will employ closed-loop, nuanced approaches that are synergistic with native physiological processes. The potential for editing human memory—decoding, enhancing, incepting, or deleting specific memories—suggests exciting therapeutic possibilities but also raises considerable ethical concerns.

attachments.name: ‘Black Mirror’ Study Guide: The Entire History of You
attachments.description: Black Mirror’ is a satirical anthology series that examines the dark aspects of modern society, particularly as it relates to our relationship with technology. Each standalone episode presents a picture of a world that’s futuristic, yet believable; cool, yet horrifying. Each of these study guides will touch on some of the themes the episode explores. Themes: Surveillance and the new age panopticon, memory and control, and living in the past.

attachments.name: Augmenting human memory using personal lifelogs
attachments.description: Memory is a key human facility to support life activities, including social interactions, life management and problem solving. Unfortunately, our memory is not perfect. Normal individuals will have occasional memory problems which can be frustrating, while those with memory impairments can often experience a greatly reduced quality of life. Augmenting memory has the potential to make normal individuals more effective, and those with significant memory problems to have a higher general quality of life. Current technologies are now making it possible to automatically capture and store daily life experiences over an extended period, potentially even over a lifetime.

attachments.name: Evolution of mediated memory in the digital age: tracing its path from the 1950s to 2010s
attachments.description: In the digital age, the relationship between human memory and media is intimate and impossible to separate. This understanding serves as the foundation for this study of mediated memory, which includes an investigation into how memory is stored, represented, and communicated via different forms of media. Despite its significance, there has yet to be a comprehensive review leading to a complete understanding of mediated memory research, particularly from the 1950s to the 2010s. This paper aims to address this knowledge gap through an extensive literature review. It examines research spanning multiple decades, focusing on the methods and paradigms used in previous mediated memory studies. The review uncovers a dual-sided representation of memory. Neurological-cognitive science research suggests that memory is represented through technology, particularly in neuroimaging techniques. Conversely, humanities and social science research highlight memory’s cultural representation through digital media, such as television, computers, smartphones, the internet, and social media. The review reveals a dichotomy in mediated memory research, with a risk of oversimplification due to the distinct paradigms. However, since the late 2000s, an interdisciplinary approach has gained momentum, leading to a more integrated perspective on mediated memory. This paper offers a comprehensive review of mediated memory studies from the 1950s to the 2010s, providing historical context, key theories, methodologies, and debates. It also identifies three distinct trajectories in these studies and highlights the gaps and issues that exist in the current research. These findings carry profound implications for future mediated memory research, advocating for a comprehensive, interdisciplinary approach to advance our understanding of how memory is shaped and represented in the digital age.

attachments.name: The Human Brain’s Data Storage May Be 2.5 Petabytes: 10 Times More Capable Than We Knew
attachments.description: John Mills Date:  October 26, 2024 For decades, scientists believed the human brain held vast but limited data storage—often compared to a few hundred terabytes, like a high-end computer. However, recent breakthroughs have upended these assumptions, revealing the brain’s data storage capacity to be potentially 10 times greater than previous estimates. This newfound understanding offers profound implications for multiple fields, from healthcare and education to artificial intelligence. In a world increasingly driven by data, these discoveries about our organic “hard drive” could inspire new solutions to age-old challenges, opening doors to memory enhancements, personalized learning, and improved neurodegenerative treatments.

description.shortText: The digital reconstruction of brain tissue enables circuit-level simulations of neural behavior, shedding light on cognitive processes, disease mechanisms, and consciousness.
description.longTextHtml:
Brain digital reconstruction involves creating highly detailed three-dimensional models of brain tissue, incorporating all neuronal types, synaptic connections, and biophysical properties. Using advanced imaging techniques such as electron microscopy and high-resolution scanning, researchers map the intricate network of neurons and their synapses. Computational models then simulate neural activity under different conditions, adjusting variables like calcium ion concentration to observe changes in brainwave patterns.

These reconstructions allow scientists to study how neural circuits function in response to stimuli, unlocking new insights into brain states such as sleep, learning, and disease progression. By revealing emergent properties that individual neurons alone cannot explain, these simulations provide a new lens through which to understand cognitive functions and neurological disorders.

Future Perspectives

A fully simulated brain could revolutionize neuroscience, offering a platform for testing new treatments for disorders like epilepsy, Alzheimer's, and schizophrenia without invasive human or animal trials. Such models could enable personalized medicine by simulating how an individual's brain would respond to specific drugs, potentially eliminating guesswork in neuropharmacology.

However, reconstructing an entire brain at a meaningful scale remains an enormous challenge. Despite progress in mapping neural connections, the unpredictable and dynamic nature of the brain—including genetic variations, spontaneous synaptic activity, and epigenetic influences—raises fundamental questions about whether a simulation can ever truly replicate the human experience. While researchers refine these models, the field may shift toward hybrid approaches, integrating biologically inspired algorithms rather than striving for perfect replication of brain structure.

The ethical implications of digital brain reconstruction are equally profound. If a simulation achieves an advanced level of complexity, could it be considered conscious? What responsibilities would society have toward such an entity? Additionally, biases in data collection and modeling could distort our understanding of cognition, potentially leading to flawed AI-driven applications in healthcare, security, and even legal decision-making.

Despite these uncertainties, brain digital reconstruction remains a crucial frontier in neuroscience, with the potential to reshape our understanding of the mind and open new pathways for medical and cognitive research.

attachments.name: UvA scientists create highly detailed 3D reconstruction of a human brain
attachments.description: An exhaustive map of the human brain has been a long-sought goal of neuroanatomists. Noninvasive imaging techniques such as magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) allow scientists to investigate the healthy living human brain but provide only limited anatomical detail. A higher level of detail can be obtained by using microscopy on brains from deceased donors, generally focusing on small brain structures imaged in 2D. Now a team led by scientists from the UvA, have combined MRI and microscopy to produce 3D images of two entire brains with a previously unmatched level of detail. Their findings have been published in the journal Science Advances.

attachments.name: A petavoxel fragment of human cerebral cortex reconstructed at nanoscale resolution
attachments.description: To fully understand how the human brain works, knowledge of its structure at high resolution is needed. Presented here is a computationally intensive reconstruction of the ultrastructure of a cubic millimeter of human temporal cortex that was surgically removed to gain access to an underlying epileptic focus. It contains about 57,000 cells, about 230 millimeters of blood vessels, and about 150 million synapses and comprises 1.4 petabytes. Our analysis showed that glia outnumber neurons 2:1, oligodendrocytes were the most common cell, deep layer excitatory neurons could be classified on the basis of dendritic orientation, and among thousands of weak connections to each neuron, there exist rare powerful axonal inputs of up to 50 synapses. Further studies using this resource may bring valuable insights into the mysteries of the human brain.

description.shortText: Also known as artificial uterus or ectogenesis, this device is designed to support extracorporeal embryo or fetus growth and development.
description.longTextHtml:
An artificial womb, also known as an artificial uterus or ectogenesis, is a device designed to support the growth and development of embryos or fetuses outside of the natural womb. It offers a potential alternative to traditional gestation within the human body (or other mammals), providing a controlled and nurturing environment for prenatal development.

This artificial environment mimics the conditions of the natural uterus. It typically consists of a fluid-filled chamber, or biobag, which serves as a substitute for the amniotic sac. The biobag contains a sterile fluid that provides a protective and nourishing environment for the developing fetus. Various parameters such as temperature, oxygen levels, and nutrient supply are carefully regulated and monitored to simulate the conditions found in the womb.

Artificial womb technology offers the possibility of providing a more controlled and supportive environment for premature babies, allowing them to continue their development until they reach a stage of maturity where they can thrive outside the womb. It could also facilitate advanced prenatal surgeries and interventions. Additionally, it could provide an alternative for couples facing infertility or reproductive challenges, same-sex couples, or single individuals who wish to have biological children. Other applications include endangered species conservation and research.

However, it is important to note that the development and implementation of artificial wombs raise ethical considerations and societal implications. Questions regarding the moral status of the fetus during ectogenesis and the long-term psychological and social impact on individuals and families need to be carefully addressed.

Future Perspectives

The act of fully developing embryos outside the body, commonly known as ectogenesis, could have the potential to alleviate uneven demands placed on women when it comes to reproduction. Disconnecting biological reproduction from the female body might drastically change society with the power to alter, in unprecedented ways, the interests, rights, and responsibilities of women, men, and the state regarding reproductive rights. It would include freeing women from their "biological destiny" placed by the patriarchal system, an idea that has been long perpetuated by virtually all cultures that interfere with both material culture and the infrastructure that surrounds future anthropology.

In an extreme scenario like extraterrestrial colonization, this technology may help enhance food production by developing healthy edible creatures without the risk of errant radiation, planetary contaminants, or microorganism-based diseases. On a brighter note, it might provide fast population growth by growing babies without the need for progenitors.

attachments.name: Equitable access to ectogenesis for sexual and gender minorities
attachments.description: As the technology for ectogenesis continues to advance, the ethical implications of such developments should be thoroughly and proactively explored. The possibility of full ectogenesis remains hypothetical at present, and myriad concerns regarding the safety and efficacy of the technology must be evaluated and addressed, while pressing moral considerations should be fully deliberated. However, it is conceivable that the technology may become sufficiently well established in the future and that eventually full ectogenesis might be deemed ethically acceptable as a reproductive alternative to gestation within a human womb under certain circumstances. If the safety and efficacy of full ectogenesis are established, if ethical dilemmas are sufficiently well addressed, and if the technology is offered as a reproductive option to cisgender heterosexual individuals or couples desiring to become parents, there is a moral obligation grounded in social justice to ensure that full ectogenesis be made available to individuals or couples identifying as members of sexual- or gender-minority groups who likewise seek to pursue parenthood. We examine the history of access to current family-building options, including assisted reproductive technology, surrogacy and adoption, for these populations and conclude that in the absence of robust empirical evidence suggesting an increased risk of harm to children of individuals and couples who identify as members of sexual- or gender-minority groups, equitable access to ectogenesis as a pathway to parenthood for sexual and gender minorities must be assured as a matter of reproductive justice.

Farther along it will lead to the total and complete manipulation of the process of the creation of life altogether. In other words, why wait nine months? Maybe you could produce a new human in one month, or maybe two months. Another issue, why wait till someone's 21? This could produce humans that could grow to be adults in maybe four years. attachments.name: Artificial Womb Technology and the Choice to Gestate Ex Utero: Is Partial Ectogenesis the Business of the Criminal Law?
attachments.description: It is frequently claimed that artificial wombs (AWs) could alleviate the burdens placed exclusively on women in reproduction. In this article, I demonstrate how AWs used for the partial gestation of preterm neonates could introduce new choices for women by changing perceptions of tolerable risks in gestation. In light of advancing medical technology, it is necessary to consider whether the current legal framework in England and Wales would support increased choice for women about alternative forms of gestation. I examine the ill-defined offence of ‘unlawfully procuring miscarriage’ in the Offences Against the Person Act 1861 and demonstrate that different conclusions about the legal significance of ending a pregnancy are evident, depending on the analytical lens adopted in interpreting ambiguities. Furthermore, I demonstrate that the defences available to pregnancy termination under the Abortion Act 1967 are too narrow to support choices about alternative forms of gestation, even if they become physically and medically possible. Therefore, we should decriminalise termination of pregnancy, or, if it is assumed that gestation is the business of the criminal law, specific reforms to the legal framework are necessary. The offence of unlawfully procuring miscarriage is too uncertain and broad, and the defences available are too restrictive.

attachments.name: Neonatal incubator or artificial womb? Distinguishing ectogestation and ectogenesis using the metaphysics of pregnancy
attachments.description: A 2017 Nature report was widely touted as hailing the arrival of the artificial womb. But the scientists involved claim their technology is merely an improvement in neonatal care. This raises an under-considered question: what differentiates neonatal incubation from artificial womb technology? Considering the nature of gestation—or metaphysics of pregnancy—(a) identifies more profound differences between fetuses and neonates/babies than their location (in or outside the maternal body) alone: fetuses and neonates have different physiological and physical characteristics; (b) characterizes birth as a physiological, mereological and topological transformation as well as a (morally relevant) change of location; and (c) delivers a clear distinction between neonatal incubation and ectogestation: the former supports neonatal physiology; the latter preserves fetal physiology. This allows a detailed conceptual classification of ectogenetive and ectogestative technologies according to which the 2017 system is not just improved neonatal incubation, but genuine ectogestation. But it is not an artificial womb, which is a term that is better put to rest. The analysis reveals that any ethical discussion involving ectogestation must always involve considerations of possible risks to the mother as well as her autonomy and rights. It also adds a third and potentially important dimension to debates in reproductive ethics: the physiological transition from fetus/gestateling to baby/neonate.

attachments.name: Artificial uterus: How close is the reality?
attachments.description: The uterus is just another organ that biomedicine will eventually replace, right? Possibly. Medicine does seem to be going in that direction. In recent years, the media have presented stories, including from this writer, that the era of motherless birth beckons, so we should begin pondering the social-political-economic consequences, as we do with all emerging biotechnologies.

attachments.name: An extra-uterine system to physiologically support the extreme premature lamb
attachments.description: In the developed world, extreme prematurity is the leading cause of neonatal mortality and morbidity due to a combination of organ immaturity and iatrogenic injury. Until now, efforts to extend gestation using extracorporeal systems have achieved limited success. Here we report the development of a system that incorporates a pumpless oxygenator circuit connected to the fetus of a lamb via an umbilical cord interface that is maintained within a closed ‘amniotic fluid’ circuit that closely reproduces the environment of the womb. We show that fetal lambs that are developmentally equivalent to the extreme premature human infant can be physiologically supported in this extra-uterine device for up to 4 weeks. Lambs on support maintain stable haemodynamics, have normal blood gas and oxygenation parameters and maintain patency of the fetal circulation. With appropriate nutritional support, lambs on the system demonstrate normal somatic growth, lung maturation and brain growth and myelination.

attachments.description: ‘Parents can look at their foetus in real time’: are artificial wombs the future? Scientists are currently pushing on an ethical boundary. Will out of body gestation ever replace the experience of human birth?

attachments.name: Artificial womb technology and clinical translation: Innovative treatment or medical research?
attachments.description: In 2017 and 2019, two research teams claimed ‘proof of principle’ for artificial womb technology (AWT). AWT has long been a subject of speculation in bioethical literature, with broad consensus that it is a welcome development. Despite this, little attention is afforded to more immediate ethical problems in the development of AWT, particularly as an alternative to neonatal intensive care. To start this conversation, I consider whether experimental AWT is innovative treatment or medical research. The research–treatment distinction, pervasive in regulation worldwide, is intended to isolate research activities and subject them to a greater degree of oversight. I argue that there is a tendency in the literature to conceptualize AWT for partial ectogenesis as innovative treatment. However, there are sufficiently serious ethical concerns with experimental AWT that mean that it must not be first used on humans on the basis that it is a ‘beneficial treatment’. First, I outline the prospects for translation of AWT animal studies into treatment for human preterms. Second, I challenge the conceptualizations of experimental AWT as innovative treatment. It must be considered medical research to reflect the investigatory nature of the process and guarantee sufficient protections for subjects. Identifying that AWT is research is crucial in formulating further ethico‐legal questions regarding the experimental use of AWT. Third, I demonstrate that clinical trials will be a necessary part of the clinical translation of AWT because of requirements laid out by regulators. I consider the justification for clinical trials and highlight some of the crucial ethical questions about the conditions under which they should proceed.

attachments.description: In order to better understand important biological membranes, it is necessary to explore new methods. Researchers at TU Wien (Vienna) have succeeded in creating an artificial placental barrier on a chip, using a high-resolution 3D printing process.

attachments.name: 3D model of human placenta developed
attachments.description: (Vienna, 03 August 2018) The placenta is the organ connecting mother and embryo. Its main functions are the exchange of nutrients, gases and metabolic products and the production of hormones and other substances essential for embryonic development. Placental malfunctions are the main cause of pregnancy complications and can lead to miscarriage and other serious disorders that endanger both mother and child. So far, the mechanisms underlying these disorders remain largely unexplained, not least because, up until now, there has been no reliable human cell culture model system. MedUni Vienna researchers have now successfully developed a 3D model of the human placenta.

attachments.name: Kick-off international project ‘Perinatal Life Support’
attachments.description: This 5-year project falls under the European Union’s Horizon 2020 FET Open Program to fund projects on new ideas for radically new future technologies. This can involve a wide range of new technological possibilities inspired by cutting-edge science. The project was coordinated by Professor Frans van de Vosse of the Eindhoven University of Technology. The project aims to develop an artificial womb to increase the chances of survival for extremely premature born babies (born between 24-28 weeks). For these babies, the chances of survival increases with each day in the artificial womb, which serves as a replacement for an incubator.

attachments.name: ‘Artificial wombs’: The science that could help premature babies
attachments.description: Teams across the world are learning about the pregnancy process to solve a number of medical challenges, including specialist incubators – known as 'artificial wombs' – to try and help premature babies survive and have longer and healthier lives.

attachments.name: Development of a miniaturized lung and kidney support device for critically ill newborns
attachments.description: The EU project "ArtPlac" is a preclinical research project to develop an innovative technology for medical treatments in neonatal intensive care. The project involves an international research team of physicians and engineers, supported by an organization that represents the interests of premature and newborn babies and their families. The Fraunhofer Institute for Biomedical Engineering IBMT is contributing its expertise in the development of microfluidic systems and sensor development and integration to the project. The aim of the project is to develop a combined lung and kidney support device for connection to the umbilical vessels. The device enables a less invasive approach than the therapies currently in use. This new approach should reduce the risk and medical burden for the newborn.

attachments.name: Artificial Wombs are Coming. Are We Ready for Their Effects?
attachments.description: Laura Johnson Dahlke’s Outer Origin: A Discourse on Ectogenesis and the Value of Human Experience is an essential read for anyone interested in artificial womb technology and its implications for humanity. She grapples with one of the most pertinent and important questions of our age: how will technology alter something as fundamental and valuable as how humans come into being? Once only the topic of science fiction, complete ectogenesis—growing offspring outside of a woman’s body from conception to full gestation—may soon become possible. Johnson Dahlke implores readers to imagine this reality mindfully.

description.shortText: A connected and collaborative mapping system that enables the seamless integration and exchange of map data between applications, devices, and services.
description.longTextHtml:
Geospatial data are accessible to a wide range of users, shareable, and compatible across diverse mapping systems and platforms. Using open standards, formats, and protocols, this solution facilitates the effortless exchange and integration of map data between applications, devices, and services.

Underpinned by the support of major technology companies and mapping institutions, Interoperable Open Map Data provide high-quality, continuously updated datasets that drive innovation across public, private, and community initiatives. By adopting common data protocols, the system enhances interoperability while reducing redundancy, lowering costs, and streamlining mapping processes.

Future Perspectives

One of the main hurdles in mapping the physical environment is the inherent complexity of the task. Interoperable Open Map Data have the potential not only to simplify this challenge but also to transform policy making, resource planning, surveying, disaster migration, and infrastructure monitoring.

Looking ahead, this technology could evolve to support real-time dynamic mapping by integrating IoT sensor networks, autonomous navigation systems, augmented reality applications, and predictive urban planning tools. As digital and physical worlds merge, novel economic models—such as decentralized location-based services and community-driven spatial innovation—may emerge, redefining urban development, disaster response, and environmental sustainability.

description.shortText: This solution harnesses advanced ad-targeting, behavior tracking, natural language processing, and adaptive engagement scripts to deliver personalized, context-aware content in real time.
description.longTextHtml:
This technology integrates ad-targeting, behavior tracking, and natural language processing with adaptive engagement scripts to generate and deliver personalized content across digital platforms. Leveraging deep learning algorithms and real-time data analytics, it can design and render thousands of tailored banners and interactive experiences per second, eliminating the reliance on traditional focus groups and fragmented datasets.

By aggregating online chatter, regional trends, and comparative data, the system predicts consumer needs and delivers targeted messaging for advertisers, public service agencies, and brands while gathering valuable feedback. Advanced machine learning models are employed to filter out spoof data and mitigate fraud, such as click injection, ensuring that genuine human preferences drive personalization. Building on industry insights regarding AI-driven personalization, this approach overcomes data silos and enhances both creative output and engagement efficiency.

However, the misapplication of this kind of technology could lead to a scenario of data mediation control and manipulation of information. It would create specific ideology-based bubbles from the perspective of both individuals and entire populations or regions. These populations would be prone to mass data collection for analysis, a process that would directly affect collective autonomy and media independence.

Future Perspectives

In a future shaped by virtual and augmented realities, Hyper-Tailored AI Communication could offer each user a uniquely immersive digital experience that adapts in real time to their emotional state and personal history. Advanced emotional AI and adaptive brand avatars might dynamically adjust tone, style, and messaging to optimize engagement and conversion, creating differentiated digital worlds based on user profiles and subscription tiers.

As ethical and regulatory frameworks evolve, this technology may foster an ecosystem where personalized communication not only boosts consumer satisfaction and economic performance but also enhances transparent public governance. With the integration of insights from neuroscience and psychology, it holds the potential to unlock unprecedented interactive storytelling, creative marketing, and even avenues for enriched democratic participation—provided that robust privacy safeguards and equitable practices are maintained.

attachments.name: AI Personalization
attachments.description: AI personalization refers to the use of artificial intelligence (AI) to tailor messaging, product recommendations and services to individual users. By analyzing data and learning from user behavior, AI-powered tools can create highly personalized encounters that enhance customer experiences and increase customer engagement.

attachments.name: Digital sovereignty or digital colonialism?
attachments.description: Beyond tensions of privacy and security, we are witnessing today a real confrontation between control and freedom, not only of the individual, but of entire populations and regions, enhanced by technologies and massive collection and analysis of data—from predicting and influencing behaviours, to the automation of public services and the ability to fully control and disrupt those services, even remotely. From gaining access to a global communications platform to losing the ability to protect the rights of those who are interconnected through those platforms. Are we witnessing a new form of digital colonialism?

description.shortText: Geolocation-based learning harnesses geofencing technology to deliver real-time, contextual educational content based on users’ precise physical location.
description.longTextHtml:
A location-based education service employs GPS, RFID, Wi-Fi, or cellular data to define virtual geofences that trigger tailored information as a mobile device or RFID tag enters or leaves designated areas. Originally popularized for marketing, this approach now transforms educational experiences by segmenting content according to where users are, whether during campus events, recruitment fairs, or while exploring a city’s historical sites.

The system relies on robust sensor integration, precise location tracking, and real-time data analytics to provide on-the-spot learning that adapts to diverse environments—from notifying about local health issues to guiding tourists with cultural narratives or assisting farmers with region-specific crop information. Emphasis on data privacy and security is critical, as similar technologies are already in use for campus safety and device protection.

Future Perspectives

As satellite internet expands and mobile device accessibility grows globally, location-based learning is poised to evolve into an even more immersive educational tool. Imagine augmented reality glasses that overlay interactive historical events or scientific data onto the physical world as students move through their environments.

Future systems may integrate wearable sensors and IoT devices to adapt content dynamically in response to environmental cues, ultimately blending physical and digital learning spaces. This convergence with AI-driven analytics and immersive technologies could not only redefine how educational content is delivered but also enhance campus security and support smart urban planning, paving the way for transformative, context-aware education across the world.

attachments.name: Place-based education – a systematic review of literature
attachments.description: Place based education (PBE) is a pedagogical approach that emphasises the connection between a learning process and the physical place in which teachers and students are located. It incorporates the meanings and the experiences of place in teaching and learning, which can extend beyond the walls of the school. PBE regained significant attention with the early 2020 outbreak of the COVID-19 pandemic, which caused large scale school closures globally and forced the rapid adoption of alternative learning environments, including teaching and learning outdoors, and learning from home. This systematic review aims to analyse English language research on PBE published in peer reviewed journals in the last twenty years. We map the themes included in this research corpus, highlight the geographical and subject specific topics where PBE is analysed, and categorise the themes that emerged from the research, according to Ardoin and colleagues’ model of PBE dimensions. (Ardoin et al. [2012]. Exploring the dimensions of place: A confirmatory factor analysis of data from three ecoregional sites. Environmental Education Research, 18(5), 583–607. https://doi.org/10.1080/13504622.2011.640930). As educators, scholars and policymakers in many countries increasingly seek to integrate PBE into curricula, a broad understanding and status check of current research directions will help steer future studies of PBE, as well as help guide education policy and practice.

attachments.name: Location-Based Learning and Its Effect on Students’ Understanding of Newton’s Laws of Motion
attachments.description: Location -based learning refers to place-based education conducted online with the use of geographic information systems and mobile devices; with the shift to distance learning, its integration in science education warrants careful evaluation. The goal of this study was to examine the effect of location-based learning on students’ understanding of Newton’s laws of motion and to characterize the learning outcomes. The participants were 373 eighth-grade students, divided into two groups: control (n = 167) — teacher-centered, textbook-oriented instruction — and experimental (n = 206) — student-centered, location-based learning. The study applied a quasi-experimental research design, within a framework of a mixed-methods approach, in which data were collected through pre- and post-questionnaires and the analysis of students’ learning outcomes. The findings indicated a significant positive effect for the location-based learning approach on students’ ability to generate and answer science-related questions, provide reasoned explanations, and connect scientific topics to daily life. Significant relationships were indicated between students’ ability to generate questions and their ability to provide reasoned explanations. The study points to the importance of engaging students in location-based learning and in the process of generating science-related questions, information points on a digital map, and multimedia features.

description.shortText: Decentralized and encrypted blockchain protocols designed to securely manage and streamline digital health data exchange.
description.longTextHtml:
A decentralized and encrypted method of distributing, sharing, and storing digital healthcare files. Cryptocurrencies and smart contracts not only facilitate secure financial transactions but also ensure that medical records remain tamper-proof, auditable, and accessible across a global network of verified nodes.

Instead of relying on a centralized database, medical information is maintained on a decentralized ledger where doctors, nurses, patients, and other stakeholders can autonomously access, update, and verify data. Enhanced interoperability is achieved through industry-standard APIs, while robust audit trails, patient consent management, and real-time data provenance tracking support regulatory compliance and accurate decision-making. This integration with existing healthcare infrastructures paves the way for improved diagnostics, personalized treatment, and more efficient knowledge exchange across regions and borders.

Future Perspectives

In the evolving landscape of digital healthcare, the blockchain system is poised to transform patient care and research by democratizing data access and fostering trust. As AI-driven diagnostics and personalized treatment plans gain traction, blockchain could serve as the secure backbone for exchanging sensitive medical information, ensuring data integrity and privacy even as the volume of information grows exponentially.

In a future marked by interconnected global health networks, this technology may empower underserved regions by bridging information gaps between urban and rural settings, thus elevating the overall quality of care. Looking ahead to 2035, a fully integrated healthcare ecosystem built on blockchain could support innovative, ethical AI algorithms and real-time epidemic monitoring, ultimately reshaping how medical knowledge is shared and how healthcare services are delivered.

description.shortText: A machine learning–driven solution that streamlines compliance procedures and audits both public and private operations.
description.longTextHtml:
Automated compliance software combines technical expertise with judicial systems to detect and prevent illicit activities by processing vast amounts of data from public and private sources. Embedded with advanced machine learning algorithms, the system efficiently audits public accounts, financial transactions, and even cryptocurrency activities through techniques such as anomaly detection, natural language processing, and predictive analytics. It examines millions of transactions to identify irregular expenditures or fraudulent operations, thereby red-flagging corruption schemes and transforming traditional financial and regulatory landscapes.

In addition, the integration of blockchain technology ensures tamper-proof record keeping, enhancing transparency and trust. By automating legal research, contract review, outcome prediction, and fraud detection, this technology facilitates more rigorous audits and empowers government agencies, institutions, and companies to engage citizens through social media, fostering a collaborative approach to regulatory oversight.

Future Perspectives

In the coming years, automated compliance could radically reshape the regulatory landscape. Beyond enforcing existing norms, future systems may evolve into self-monitoring ecosystems that integrate smart contracts and blockchain-based records to codify environmental and financial regulations. As these technologies mature, deep-learning techniques might even predict behavioral patterns and political missteps, reducing the likelihood of regulatory breaches and corruption.

This transformation would not only make audits public and participatory but also drive governments to digitize and standardize their data. However, the widespread implementation of such transparent systems raises new challenges, particularly in balancing public accountability with individual privacy. As research continues on standardizing environmental data exchange and regulatory codification, automated compliance stands at the frontier of a digital revolution in governance.

attachments.name: Automated compliance checking using building information models
attachments.description: Building designs in the UK are currently checked manually against a frequently changing and increasingly complex set of building regulations. This is a major task for both designers and enforcers, often leading to ambiguity, inconsistency in assessments and delays in the overall construction process. Technical developments in Building Information Modelling (BIM) offer the potential for a new generation of software tools that can automate the checking of compliance with building codes, thus improving the efficiency of building design and procurement. To attain these efficiencies designers must change their working practices and move away from the definition of a building in multiple and disparate documents to a single coherent building model from which the documentation is generated. Theoretically, this building model could contain sufficient information to respond to interrogation at the level of building code compliance, though in practice only a percentage of the required information is normally present. This paper reviews previous research into automated code compliance, identifies the key issues for future development and examines the causes of information paucity for compliance checking in the current generation of BIM tools.

description.shortText: Bias detection algorithms equipped with fairness metrics and adversarial de-biasing techniques can uncover and mitigate systematic discrimination in machine learning models.
description.longTextHtml:
As machine learning infiltrates society, it has become evident that even advanced algorithms can perpetuate historical biases. Algorithmic Bias Detection Tools are designed to scan the entire machine learning pipeline—from data collection and training to deployment—to identify and quantify the influence of sensitive variables such as race, gender, class, and religion. By employing quantitative fairness metrics like statistical parity, equal opportunity, and disparate impact, these systems generate clear, actionable insights into where biases arise.

A popular method, adversarial de-biasing, works by removing discriminatory signals from latent model representations during training. Complemented by interactive visualization dashboards, the tool enables researchers and practitioners to monitor model outcomes in real time and recommend targeted adjustments to mitigate bias.

Furthermore, integrating such technical measures with the broader practice of diversifying development teams reinforces a holistic approach to reducing systemic inequities. In doing so, this technology not only enhances model transparency and accountability but also aligns with emerging global regulatory standards on algorithmic fairness.

Future Perspectives

Looking ahead, the role of bias detection tools may evolve from reactive auditing to proactive guardians of ethical AI. Imagine a future where these systems autonomously predict and neutralize bias before models are fully deployed—serving as an embedded ethical auditor across diverse digital ecosystems. With advancements such as quantum computing and self-learning algorithms, future iterations could analyze complex, multi-dimensional bias patterns in real time, adapting continuously to new data and societal norms. Such innovations might even support policy-making by providing real-time feedback to regulators and organizations, ensuring that technological progress does not inadvertently widen social disparities. This transformative potential could redefine trust in algorithmic decision-making, paving the way for a digital future where fairness is an integral, self-sustaining feature of every AI system.

Algorithm Audit combines quantitative and qualitative methods to make normative decisions about fair AI, also known as our joint fairness assessment method (JFAM).

This way, they’re better equipped to debias their current practices and improve their overall decision-making.

attachments.name: Data-Centric Factors in Algorithmic Fairness
attachments.description: Notwithstanding the widely held view that data generation and data curation processes are prominent sources of bias in machine learning algorithms, there is little empirical research seeking to document and understand the specific data dimensions affecting algorithmic unfairness. Contra the previous work, which has focused on modeling using simple, small-scale benchmark datasets, we hold the model constant and methodically intervene on relevant dimensions of a much larger, more diverse dataset. For this purpose, we introduce a new dataset on recidivism in 1.5 million criminal cases from courts in the U.S. state of Wisconsin, 2000-2018. From this main dataset, we generate multiple auxiliary datasets to simulate different kinds of biases in the data. Focusing on algorithmic bias toward different race/ethnicity groups, we assess the relevance of training data size, base rate difference between groups, representation of groups in the training data, temporal aspects of data curation, including race/ethnicity or neighborhood characteristics as features, and training separate classifiers by race/ethnicity or crime type. We find that these factors often do influence fairness metrics holding the classifier specification constant, without having a corresponding effect on accuracy metrics. The methodology and the results in the paper provide a useful reference point for a data-centric approach to studying algorithmic fairness in recidivism prediction and beyond.

description.shortText: By leveraging quantum dynamics and ultra-cold atoms as an alternative to GPS updates, this technology can suggest the the best route to reduce travel times and provide a more accurate estimated time of arrival without the need for satellites.
description.longTextHtml:
A quantum compass is an advanced navigation instrument that measures relative position using atom interferometry. Unlike conventional navigation systems that rely on Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS), such as GPS, a quantum compass operates independently of satellites. It harnesses high-precision atomic accelerometers and gyroscopes, which exploit quantum superposition to detect minute changes in movement with exceptional accuracy.

Quantum sensors utilize ultra-cold atoms and laser-based measurement techniques to track motion through gravitational and inertial variations. This allows for continuous, self-contained positioning, making the system immune to satellite signal interference, jamming, or blackouts. Predictive analytics and machine learning algorithms further enhance navigation precision by optimizing routes and reducing operational costs.

This technology has broad applications, ranging from military operations—where GPS denial environments are a challenge—to maritime, aviation, underground and autonomous vehicles. For example, it can help ships navigate more accurately in deep-sea environments, provide pinpoint accuracy for aircraft and drones, and ensure reliable troop positioning.

Future Perspectives

Conventional GPS is increasingly vulnerable to signal jamming and obstructions, posing economic and security risks. Studies suggest that a single day of satellite disruption could cost the UK alone over £1 billion, highlighting the urgent need for resilient alternatives. Quantum navigation offers a robust, interference-proof solution, making it a strategic priority for governments, defence sectors, and transportation industries.

The rise of autonomous vehicles will further amplify the demand for precise, satellite-independent navigation. Quantum compasses could become a standard feature in logistics and urban mobility, allowing for real-time traffic optimization, route efficiency, and improved energy consumption. Additionally, smart cities could integrate quantum-based positioning systems into their infrastructure, enhancing public transportation, emergency response coordination, and air traffic management.

As research continues, the miniaturization and commercialization of quantum navigation systems will drive their adoption across multiple industries, reshaping how we perceive and interact with location-based services in the future.

Bias-free sensors based on atom interferometers have been proposed, but they generally lack sufficient bandwidth for navigation. To solve this problem, the authors hybridize an atom interferometer with a classical accelerometer, using an approach based on Kalman filtering that provides optimal, robust estimation of the classical accelerometer's bias, even in a harsh environment. This approach can readily be extended to other types of atom interferometers, such as gyrometers or gradiometers.

Our results indicate that quantum sensing will be a critical enabler of future smart cities, generating advanced monitoring, control, and decision-making capabilities across various sectors. description.shortText: A highly secure, encrypted database designed to safeguard e-citizen data from cyberattacks, geopolitical threats, and natural disasters. Operating under sovereign rights like a traditional embassy, it is hosted in a foreign jurisdiction, ensuring the digital continuity of a nation's critical infrastructure and enabling rapid recovery in emergencies.
description.longTextHtml:
A data backup embassy is a sovereign, transnational digital infrastructure that protects sensitive government and citizen data from cyberattacks, espionage, and force majeure events. It functions as a cloud-based extension of a country's digital services, ensuring continuity in the event of large-scale disruptions.

The system operates on highly encrypted, redundant storage servers located outside the country's borders but remains under the legal jurisdiction of the home nation. This ensures full sovereignty over the stored data while benefiting from additional security and stability in a foreign location. In the case of a large-scale cyberattack, the embassy can reboot critical government functions almost instantaneously, restoring access to essential digital services like healthcare records, tax systems, and corporate registries.

Beyond cyber resilience, a data backup embassy also mitigates risks from natural disasters, power grid failures, or military conflicts that could compromise domestic data centers. However, the deployment of such infrastructure raises significant legal and ethical challenges. International laws currently lack standardized frameworks to regulate transnational government data storage, particularly in areas such as privacy, access rights, and emergency data retrieval protocols. Global cooperation will be necessary to develop agreements that balance security, transparency, and individual data rights.

Future Perspectives

The centralization of vast amounts of national data in a single physical location presents potential risks, making the system an attractive target for both cyberattacks and geopolitical interference. To address this, future iterations of data embassies could adopt decentralized and distributed ledger technologies, such as blockchain, to create a globally dispersed, tamper-resistant backup system. This would ensure that no single entity could compromise national data integrity.

In addition, AI-driven cybersecurity measures could automate threat detection and response, proactively neutralizing intrusion attempts before they escalate into system-wide breaches. Advanced cryptographic techniques, such as homomorphic encryption, could allow secure data processing without exposing raw information, further strengthening privacy protections.

Looking further ahead, DNA-based data storage could revolutionize the way nations preserve digital archives. Capable of encoding petabytes of information in microscopic biological structures, this technology could provide an ultra-dense, durable, and cyberattack-resistant solution for long-term data preservation. While still in its infancy, DNA storage could eliminate traditional hacking vulnerabilities, ensuring the ultimate resilience of national digital assets.

description.shortText: A privacy-preserving encryption method that allows data to be processed without being decrypted.
description.longTextHtml:
Homomorphic encryption is a cryptographic technique that enables computations to be performed directly on encrypted data. Unlike traditional encryption methods, where data must be decrypted before use — posing potential security risks — homomorphic encryption ensures that data remains protected even during processing. This capability is particularly valuable in contexts where sensitive information is outsourced to third parties, such as cloud computing services.

At its core, this technology leverages advanced mathematical functions to allow algebraic operations on ciphertexts, generating encrypted results that, once decrypted, match the outcome of operations performed on the original plaintexts. There are several types of homomorphic encryption schemes, including partially, somewhat, and fully homomorphic encryption (FHE), each offering different balances of computational power and efficiency.

Homomorphic encryption is currently being explored across various sectors. In healthcare, it facilitates secure sharing and analysis of patient records; in finance, it allows encrypted transactions to be analyzed for fraud detection; in cloud computing, it enables data analytics on encrypted datasets without ever exposing the raw information.

Future Perspectives

In the long term, homomorphic encryption could transform how society handles trust and confidentiality in the digital realm. It may enable a future where data privacy is inherently preserved in every transaction, eliminating the need for intermediaries and reducing vulnerability to cyberattacks. Secure federated learning models could train artificial intelligence on encrypted user data across devices, without ever accessing individual records — redefining data sovereignty.

Governments might use homomorphic encryption to run statistical models on citizen data without violating individual privacy. In journalism or activism under authoritarian regimes, this technology could provide a lifeline for whistleblowers, allowing their data to be processed without being revealed. Eventually, homomorphic encryption could be foundational to building decentralized systems that operate transparently while maintaining individual confidentiality at scale.

attachments.name: Fully Homomorphic Encryption
attachments.description: Customer data privacy is a fundamental need for maintaining human trust and reputation in digital business services, and data encryption is key to preserving this privacy. With traditional encryption methods, data is encrypted while at rest and in-flight, but must be decrypted to be accessed for computing and business-critical operations. During the decryption process, sensitive data becomes vulnerable to internal and external risk of data exfiltration and other cyberthreats. With Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE), data remains securely encrypted -- even during computations. With FHE, data is always encrypted and can be shared, even onto untrusted domains in the cloud, while remaining unreadable by those doing the computation.  The journey begins with encrypting your sensitive data (PII, PHI) and algorithms (AI, ML) with IBM Fully Homomorphic Encryption. attachments.name: Revisiting Fully Homomorphic Encryption Schemes
attachments.description: Homomorphic encryption is a sophisticated encryption technique that allows computations on encrypted data to be done without the requirement for decryption. This trait makes homomorphic encryption appropriate for safe computation in sensitive data scenarios, such as cloud computing, medical data exchange, and financial transactions. The data is encrypted using a public key in homomorphic encryption, and the calculation is conducted on the encrypted data using an algorithm that retains the encryption. The computed result is then decrypted with a private key to acquire the final output. This abstract notion protects data while allowing complicated computations to be done on the encrypted data, resulting in a secure and efficient approach to analysing sensitive information. This article is intended to give a clear idea about the various fully Homomorphic Encryption Schemes present in the literature and analyse and compare the results of each of these schemes. description.shortText: Cryptographic systems that verify data without revealing it, enabling privacy-preserving digital interactions.
description.longTextHtml:
Zero-Knowledge Proof (ZKP) infrastructure is a cryptographic framework that allows one party (the prover) to prove to another (the verifier) that a specific statement is true without disclosing any additional information beyond the validity of the statement itself. The core mechanism relies on complex mathematical protocols that ensure the integrity and confidentiality of data during verification.

In practical terms, ZKPs enable secure transactions, identity verification, and data authentication without exposing sensitive inputs. For example, in financial services, ZKPs can prove that a user has sufficient funds without showing their entire account balance. In identity systems, a person can prove they meet age or nationality requirements without revealing their full identity. ZKPs are increasingly integrated into blockchain technologies to ensure scalability and confidentiality, as seen in protocols like zk-SNARKs and zk-STARKs.

Applications are growing across sectors: from enhancing privacy in public blockchains, to protecting user data in decentralized identity systems, and ensuring regulatory compliance without intrusive oversight. The technology is still evolving, but its foundational role in privacy-preserving computation is clear.

Future Perspectives

In the long term, Zero-Knowledge Proof Infrastructure could become a foundation of global digital governance, enabling a new class of trustless systems. Entire economies might operate on architectures where authentication, compliance, and accountability are maintained without requiring exposure of private data. This could transform sectors like finance, healthcare, and public administration, where data confidentiality and integrity are both paramount.

Imagine borderless digital identities that individuals can carry throughout their lives, proving qualifications, age, or residency with a single click — while disclosing nothing unnecessary. In AI systems, ZKPs might enable audit trails of decision-making processes without revealing proprietary models or training data. As quantum computing advances, post-quantum ZKP protocols could be crucial to future-proofing privacy in the face of new computational threats.

The wide adoption of ZKP infrastructures might eventually establish a new social contract in the digital realm: one that assumes privacy by default and trust through proof—not exposure.

attachments.name: Scaling DeFi with ZK Rollups: Design, Deployment, and Evaluation of a Real-Time Proof-of-Concept
attachments.description: Ethereum’s scalability limitations pose significant challenges for the adoption of decentralized applications (dApps). Zero-Knowledge Rollups (ZK Rollups) present a promising solution, bundling transactions off-chain and submitting validity proofs on-chain to enhance throughput and efficiency. In this work, we examine the technical underpinnings of ZK Rollups and stress test their performance in real-world applications in decentralized finance (DeFi). We set up a proof-of-concept (PoC) consisting of ZK rollup and decentralized exchange, and implement load balancer generating token swaps. Our results show that the rollup can process up to 71 swap transactions per second, compared to 12 general transaction by Ethereum. We further analyze transaction finality trade-offs with related security concerns, and discuss the future directions for integrating ZK Rollups into Ethereum’s broader ecosystem.

attachments.name: Zero-Knowledge Proofs — What Are They and Why Do They Matter?
