attachments.name: Bio-based additives for thermoplastics
attachments.description: Presently, there are significant research efforts being undertaken to produce bio-based chemicals in a cost-effective way. The polymer chemists and engineers are no exception to this. Additives for polymers correspond to a large section of the plastics market and bio-based products can substitute many of them. The scientific literature has a large number of publications focusing on the preparation and testing of bio-based polymer additives; however, the small number of products that reach the market, which are bio-based, does not reflect this. In terms of the global market, the environmentally friendly appeal of bio-based additives alone is not sufficient; the bio-based product must have similar or better performance than the oil-based and be comparable or lower in cost than the existing products. In this review, we focus on bio-based polymer additives that have already reached the market or have a real possibility of reaching the market in a cost-effective way.

description.shortText: Artificial apiary that creates a constant spring-like environment for bees in urban settings that can help save honeybees from extinction.
description.longTextHtml:
A synthetic apiary which creates a controlled space in which seasonal honeybees can thrive year-round. Light, humidity, and temperature are engineered to simulate a perpetual spring environment. Also, undisturbed by external stimuli that may be found in urban environments, bees are provided with synthetic pollen and sugar water, while being regularly evaluated for health and well-being. After succeeding in the adaptation phase, in which the queen is able to lay her eggs in the apiary, the other bees will be able to function normally in the artificial environment.

Soon, this technology will allow hives to be integrated into urban planning, attaching them to buildings despite extreme weather conditions. Long-term goals include developing new ways of allowing bees and humans to cohabitate and create further understanding of the factors that influence hive building and structure. This outcome reveals that natural cultivation in artificial spaces could be possible across scales, from organisms to building-scale.

Bees, as agents of cross-pollination, are an essential part of our agricultural production. However, their health and population have declined over the past decade due, in large part, to environmental conditions and exposure to pesticides. By creating a controlled environment in urban settings that can help establish and support bee colonies, we might be able to preserve the natural environmental balance they create as one of the most important species on the planet.

Future perspectives

Synthetic Apiary Environments could be a complementary technology to other areas such as Vertical Farming or urban agriculture in general – bees could simultaneously pollinate horticultural crops while providing an urban source of honey for local communities or restaurants. If this kind of experiment succeeds, it could be readapted to take care of other endangered species vital to sustaining life on Earth, such as fungi, earthworms, and ants.

description.shortText: Interactive storytelling software that uses machine learning to recognize behavior patterns, and revises narratives using emotion-based experiences. By computationally predicting the emotional response to a narrative segment, this system could expand human interaction with digital content.
description.longTextHtml:
Data analytics and machine learning, applied as story creation tools, combining content creation, emotional curves, sentiment analysis, and video synthesis. Capable of making assumptions based on past and real-time collected data, this technology can predict future emotional responses and generate storytelling based on human emotion.

Spectators and listeners are exposed to a webcam powered by AI and skin-conductivity sensors that process, analyze, learn, and make assumptions at a scale and depth of detail impossible for individual human analysts. The data gathered routes back into the software, and the narrative of a game or a story changes based on the emotional inputs provided by the user.

The software provides storylines, such as characters, plots, relationships, and scenarios, that adapt to how audiences respond to those inputs. By computationally predicting the emotional response to a narrative segment, this system can influence both the storyline and keep the user on a dynamic curve of interactions.

Future Perspectives

AI-generated narratives, plus AI capabilities of reading and reacting to emotions, could increase the effectiveness of learning processes, augmenting engagement upon recognition of positive emotional reactions. These changes could herald a new empathetic and responsive future for storytelling, where viewers or players are encouraged to bring about changes to the narrative while learning about different topics and their behaviors.

Additionally, this solution could be equally valuable for therapeutic purposes, such as helping mental health professionals identify sources of trauma by increasingly exposing subjects to patients and adjusting to their psychological responses and needs.

attachments.name: Emotion-Based Interactive Storytelling with Artificial Intelligence
attachments.description:
Artificial Intelligence (AI) techniques have been widely used
in video games to control non-playable characters. More recently,
AI has been applied to automated story generation and
game-mastering: managing the player’s experience in an interactive
narrative on-the-fly. Such methods allow the narrative
to be generated dynamically, in response to the player’s
in-game actions. As a result, it is more difficult for the human
game designers to ensure that each possible narrative trajectory
will elicit desired emotional response from the player.
We tackle this problem by computationally predicting the
player’s emotional response to a narrative segment. We use
the predictions within an AI experience manager to shape the
narrative dynamically during the game to keep the player on
an author-supplied target emotional curve.

attachments.name: Affective Story-morphing: Manipulating Shelley’s Frankenstein under program control using Emotionally Intelligent Agents
attachments.description:
We present a theoretical model for the automated generation of
plot-consistent, novel, engaging narratives based on a broad, computable model
of emotion. We review the background theory, relevant to the morphing of
narratives, composed of 28 emotion categories, 24 emotion intensity variables,
and ~400 channels for emotion expression, and which has been implemented in
an AI program called the Affective Reasoner. We argue that what is primarily of
interest in narratives is the emotion fabric in the interaction between
characters—much of which can be manipulated by the Affective Reasoner—and
that while keeping the plot the same or similar we can, under computational
control, create novel, interesting, consistent new stories that make sense to
human observers. We present and explain preliminary examples and then apply
the story-morphing techniques to a passage from Mary Shelley’s Frankenstein.

attachments.name: Capturing User Emotions in Interactive Stories: Comparing a Diegetic and a Non-diegetic Approach to Self-reporting Emotion
attachments.description: Capturing the player’s emotions in an interactive story can serve many purposes, such as to understand player response to a story or to alter the story’s path. The concept of diegesis defines the boundary between the story world and the real world, and has been used to explore different ways of conceptualizing user interface (UI) elements in interactive media. This paper explores methods of capturing players’ emotions during an interactive story and the concept of diegesis. Specifically, we posit that whether emotion capture exists in a diegetic versus a non-diegetic space can affect its accuracy when capturing player emotion. We developed two interactive stories with two emotion capture methods, one using a diegetic approach, and the other using a non-diegetic approach. We conducted a study with 64 participants to compare the two emotion capture approaches. Our results show that a diegetic approach leads to a better story experience, but that a non-diegetic approach leads to the player’s emotion being captured more accurately. We discuss the implications of the study results for integrating emotion capture in the design of interactive stories.

description.shortText: Implants and wearables that deliver artificially synaesthetic experiences by translating sensory input in a different modality from the original stimuli, allowing users to see, hear or feel things that would not otherwise be detected by normal human senses.
description.longTextHtml:
These implants and wearables are designed to enhance or substitute perceptual ability, allowing the user to see, hear or feel things that would not otherwise be detected by normal human senses. A set of algorithms translate inputs from sensors such as microphones or cameras into other sensations, e.g. sound into touch or color into sound.

This technological solution uses infrared goggles, parabolic microphones, and thermal sensors. Although these devices enhance human perception, the brain is usually still aware that it is being fed information through a piece of hardware and doesn't interpret this data in the same way it would have when the information comes from a natural sensory organ. The brain is the organ responsible for perceptual information processing, independent of the source and, through neural plasticity, it can rewire itself to substitute sensory information from one sense with that of another. With new devices and improvements in brain-machine interfaces, technological developments are reaching a point at which it is becoming possible to fool the brain into perceiving artificial sensory information as if it were part of its own natural sensory repertoire.

Besides augmenting human senses, such wearables work as devices for sensory substitution or addition. Therefore, people with disabilities could perceive the world differently by using their other senses. Colorblind individuals, as well as blind people, could hear colors as sound frequencies sent to their ears or electrical signals directly to their brains. For disabled individuals, using sensory substitution could make it easier to participate in educational experiences created for individuals without disabilities. For example, a vest with vibration engines in different parts of the body could translate spoken words into patterns, allowing users to understand what is being said as their brains are subconsciously translating the complicated vibration patterns into language.

Future Perspectives

Once brain-machine interfaces become more sophisticated, sensory substitution without having to take a detour through existing human senses could become a reality by routing information directly to the brain. Encoding sensory information in a way that the brain can understand will likely require techniques based on machine learning, incorporating feedback from the brain to co-adaptively learn how to present the information to the brain.

Patients who have suffered the loss of eyesight or who were naturally born blind could receive neural implants resulting in the ability to see, maybe even in the infrared and ultra-violet ranges and beyond. With the ability to project images directly into the visual cortex, a whole new level of immersive experiences could be reached. Also, combined with smart drugs or supplements, this type of effect could be achieved without intrusive methods such as implants or wearables. As pharmaceutical technology develops, chemicals could be combined with implants to give the user a desired and controlled sensory substitution without suffering adverse side effects.

By exchanging or amplifying human senses, a new way of perceiving the world through synesthesia could lead to a novel interpretation of reality and what it means to be human. Implantable devices could give humans abilities of other animals, or ones that do not exist in nature at all, allowing humans to “feel” electromagnetic fields, stock-market data, or even the weather when in space. In the end, the metaphorical sixth sense could become a reality.

The interface would serve as a translator, converting between the electrochemical language used by neurons in the brain and the ones and zeros that constitute the language of information technology. attachments.name: Sensory substitution: Using a vibrotactile device to orient and walk to targets.
attachments.description: This study investigates how active exploration helps users of sensory substitution devices (SSDs) to detect action-relevant information. A vibrotactile SSD was developed that generates stimulation that is contingent on the users’ movements. Target direction was specified by the location of the vibratory stimulation, and target distance by the size and intensity of the pattern of stimulation. A series of experiments was performed with blindfolded participants. In Experiments 1a to 1c, participants used the SSD to align their central body axis with prespecified targets. These experiments differed in the number of actuators that were used and whether online perception–action coupling was present. In Experiment 2, participants approached targets with forward locomotion along a straight line. Experiment 3 combined the previous experiments and studied the concomitant walking and steering toward targets. Oscillatory movements, which facilitated information pickup, were observed in all experiments. The exploratory oscillations were shown to depend on the online perception–action coupling and were related to cases of hyperacuity, for which absolute errors were found to be smaller than the areas of sensitivity of the actuators. It is concluded that, to improve the utility of SSDs, future research with SSDs should pay more attention to the role of active information detection. description.shortText: A robot powered by AI software capable of carrying out a variety of in-home tasks, such as cleaning and cooking. Equipped with wireless network and voice-identification patterns, the robot is able to perform tasks with no human oversight, while interacting with smart-home devices.
description.longTextHtml:
Specialized robots are already making their way into homes all over the world, helping with tasks such as mopping, vacuuming, and lawn-mowing. Now, more general robots are able to help with a variety of tasks, using abilities similar to those of a human being.

By using cutting-edge artificial intelligence technology, these robots are able to clean the whole house by themselves. This includes not only the cleaning itself but also recognizing and remembering where people are and the location of objects in the home. Advanced robotics allows the robot to be able to handle objects, properly managing them for each needed task, such as making coffee and cooking.

Equipped with wireless network standards and the ability to be controlled by voice commands, the robot is able to perform tasks with no human oversight, while interacting with smart-home devices. It even has a safety module, which enables the robot to recognize and react to emergency situations, such as a person falling or undergoing a seizure.

Future Perspectives

Robotic companions, especially those that help with in-home tasks, will eventually be a reality in many households. They could greatly reduce the amount of time spent with those chores, freeing up time for leisure or work-related activities. In addition, as their ability to communicate improves, they could be seen as great companions for those who are usually alone at home or for people who require care.

In more traditional cultures, household robots also have the potential to shift home relationship dynamics, taking away from women the burden of being responsible for home care, which could mean a major cultural and economic shift regarding social inequality.

description.shortText: An augmentation method able to create micro-pores in the skin in a minimally invasive manner to deliver effective ingredients with enhanced absorption rates.
description.longTextHtml:
A physical enhancement method that creates micro-pores in the skin in a minimally invasive manner to deliver effective ingredients with enhanced absorption rates. The patch composition naturally dissolves on the skin following use. These patches can be used efficiently in cosmetics given their patient usability, safety, and effectiveness.

Self-dissolving and biodegradable microneedle technologies for transdermal sustained delivery of drugs and vaccines are commonly used in medical treatments. The success of these delivery systems in medical care treatments is inspiring the cosmetic industry to do the same. Ongoing research is successfully loading skincare components into biodegradable dissolving micro-needles in order to produce novel cosmetic patches.

Although some components are extremely common in cosmetics, such as collagen or hyaluronic acid (that has strong moisturizing effects due to its high capacity to hold water), they also have difficulty penetrating the skin because of the large size of the individual molecules.

Future Perspectives

The future advancement of microneedle development will contribute to the engineering of smart microneedles that can control the release of various active ingredients under various conditions, in line with the dynamic physicochemical changes of the skin. Moreover, novel microneedle patch delivery systems with needles that can effectively release specific active ingredients to the deeper layers of the skin could potentially be part of complex skin therapies. They would administer specific probiotic and living prebiotic mixtures that can be released at given conditions to support the targeted rebalancing of specific bacteria of the microbiome inhabiting the various skin layers.

attachments.name: Living Bacterial Microneedles for Fungal Infection Treatment
attachments.description: Fungal infections are everlasting health challenges all over the world, bringing about great financial and medical burdens. Here, inspired by the natural competition law of beneficial bacteria against other microbes, we present novel living microneedles (LMNs) with functionalized bacteria encapsulation for efficient fungal infection treatment. The chosen beneficial bacterial components, Bacillus subtilis (B. subtilis), which are naturally found on the human skin and widely used for food processing, can get nutrients from the skin and escape from the immune system with the help of microneedles. Besides, the encapsulated B. subtilis can continuously produce and secrete various potential antifungal agents which can directly bind to fungal cell surface-associated proteins and destruct the cell membranes, thus avoiding drug resistance. After immobilization in the LMNs, the bacteria can stay within the LMNs without invasion and the encapsulated bacteria together with microneedles can be removed after application. Thus, the side effects, especially the risk for subsequent bacterial infections, are controlled to a minimum to ensure security. In addition, strong penetrability of the microneedles enhances penetration of antifungal agents, and their heights can be adjusted according to the infected depth to acquire better therapeutic effects. These features make the LMNs potentially valuable for clinical applications.

description.shortText: A category of buildings with a near-zero or zero net energy consumption, as well as zero on-site carbon emissions.
description.longTextHtml:
A construction system, able to reduce operational carbon emissions through buildings that consume the same amount of energy they produce. To generate energy on-site, this model takes into account the local ecosystem for the best microgeneration technologies, including photovoltaics, wind turbines, small-scale hydropower, or even other renewable sources, such as waste heat from large-scale power generation.

One of the biggest challenges in the energy sector today is balancing power supply and demand during peak times, which zero-energy buildings could alleviate. However, regulatory frameworks are still inconsistent and/or incompatible with each other when it comes to energy pricing and a sufficient incentive effect on sustainable and manageable energy production is still lacking. Emergent regulatory practices need to address these issues, including factors such as resource cycle, impact on land use, the environment, water, and human health.

Future Perspectives

With the growing demand for decarbonization, one promising solution for cost reduction and market acceleration is to plan zero energy districts. Expanding the context to a district scale may require intense and sophisticated planning from scratch, resulting in high initial costs. Yet, in the long term, it can yield many benefits that are not possible with individual zero energy buildings, such as scale effects to drive down costs per unit, shared power infrastructure, and general cost-effective energy.

As a result, a multi-objective model is developed to identify the best combination of materials and construction options considering their related costs, energy efficiency, and environmental impacts of buildings, simultaneously. This sustainable model is presented to construct a building considering the construction costs and energy consumption of the design options. To design the NZEB, while minimizing costs and carbon emissions, use has been made of a combination of different types of active/heating and cooling systems and renewable equipment through such high-efficiency, effective, and updated technologies as the solar panel. Finally, the case study of a residential building with two scenarios is used to demonstrate the proposed framework. The results show that, for scenarios1 and 2 respectively using insulation thickness such as (wall, roof, and windows) and renewable equipment have the highest sustainable impact in NEBZ's performance.

Future Perspectives

The solution has the potential to improve surgical planning as well as clinical efficacy. With advances in 3D printing and the incorporation of patient-specific anatomy, Virtual Simulation Surgery modernizes biomedical training, strengthening surgeons' skill sets, which could decrease hospital costs, improve patient outcomes, and may replace the need for and use of live animals in medical school curricula and skills-training programs.

description.shortText: By combining computational fluid dynamics with machine learning and meteorological data-sources, this system steadily improves the ability and accuracy to forecast both weather and natural incidents with far-reaching results for individuals and businesses.
description.longTextHtml:
By combining computational fluid dynamics with machine learning and meteorological data-sources, a predictive weather system provides a more accurate alternative to current weather prediction models. This dynamic and fluid forecast software aggregates a multitude of climate and weather-related data. This data is later rated, ranked, and weighted by machine learning to process immediate comparisons between historical data and weather forecasts. Used in this way, weather models could more efficiently take into account inaccuracies, such as overestimated rain predictions or even to perform more accurate predictions.

Apart from developing rankings, machine-learning models that use deep learning show promising results in predicting cyclones, atmospheric rivers, weather fronts, and forest fires, and can even assess deforestation. With better predictions of climate, it may be possible to modify decisions to decrease undesirable impacts and take better advantage of expected favorable conditions.

Farmers, for instance, could be better prepared to make decisions regarding crop management with the inclusion of the ideal window for sowing, fertilizing, weeding, and harvesting. In the case of urban planners, simulation models can be useful to adapt both existing projects and upcoming developments in order to make them more responsive to the consequences of climate change (for instance, reducing heat islands and adaptation of areas prone to flood), as well as more accountable to the measurements and policies that regulate emissions.

Future Perspectives

Gathering and processing high-quality data of potential environmental risks will continuously be a need for both future and present-day society. Improving accuracy in weather prediction can have far-reaching implications, not just for disaster mitigation, but also for businesses that rely on commodity futures trading or other weather-based factors. Due to the amount of data that needs to be analyzed, advancements in the quantum computing area should directly impact the accuracy of these forecasting systems.

Also, by combining this software with new infrared remote atmospheric sounding systems with cloud-penetrating microwave radiometers, space-borne radar, light detection and ranging (LiDAR), as well as remote sensing observations from the ground, it could create a sensor web around the globe for future views of the Earth. These new and improved weather and climate products are also leading to new industries, like “weather derivatives.” Weather derivatives are financial solutions that help weather-sensitive companies spread out and insure themselves against their inherent risks.

attachments.name: Forecasting Climatic Trends Using Neural Networks: An Experimental Study Using Global Historical Data
attachments.description: Climate change is undoubtedly one of the biggest problems in the 21st century. Currently, however, most research efforts on climate forecasting are based on mechanistic, bottom-up approaches such as physics-based general circulation models and earth system models. In this study, we explore the performance of a phenomenological, top-down model constructed using a neural network and big data of global mean monthly temperature. By generating graphical images using the monthly temperature data of 30 years, the neural network system successfully predicts the rise and fall of temperatures for the next 10 years. Using LeNet for the convolutional neural network, the accuracy of the best global model is found to be 97.0%; we found that if more training images are used, a higher accuracy can be attained. We also found that the color scheme of the graphical images affects the performance of the model. Moreover, the prediction accuracy differs among climatic zones and temporal ranges. This study illustrated that the performance of the top-down approach is notably high in comparison to the conventional bottom-up approach for decadal-scale forecasting. We suggest using artificial intelligence-based forecasting methods along with conventional physics-based models because these two approaches can work together in a complementary manner.

archive.name: Non-Fungible Token

description.shortText: A type of crypto token that is not interchangeable or replicable. It is used to represent scarcity items in virtual environments, in which the currency is the desired item itself.
description.longTextHtml:
Commonly known as NFTs, non-fungible tokens are unique digital items that can be sold, traded, and stored within the blockchain. The name "fungible" is derived from the fungibility of exchanging physical objects without modifying their value. The creation of NFTs is a way to ensure the uniqueness of a digital asset because it cannot be replicable and copied, which creates a limited availability of a commodity. When an item is non-fungible, its value is intrinsically connected to the item itself.

The use of non-fungible tokens within the gaming ecosystem is becoming ever more popular. It solves a fundamental problem regarding ownership of in-game goods. When a player buys an item inside a specific game, even if such an item costs money, it cannot be owned by the buyer because if the game developers decide to discontinue the platform, all in-game items will be lost. If the item is stored in the blockchain in the form of an NFT, it becomes genuinely possessed by the player, and it will continue to exist outside the game. In some cases, it is even possible to create trans-game assets.

As NFTs represent a big market for collectible digital goods, artists are also taking advantage of NFTs to tokenize artworks to ensure ownership and distinctiveness to the pieces. Another possible use-case for such tokens is for the tokenization of physical assets, as it creates a digital counterpart of the physical good. Thanks to the immutability of blockchains, the tokenization of physical goods could be used to replace contracts automatically.

Future Perspectives

As we move to the digitalization of physical goods, more and more users will become familiar with new forms of buying and selling such items. Prestige items, such as luxury fragrances, will be encoded into NFT through novel artworks created from perfumes and fused to their physical counterparts. These NFTs will be part of large-scale campaigns to accompany a limited rollout of an exclusive prestige category item. Each limited edition NFT artwork works as a unique blockchain asset and the form of non-interchangeable cryptocurrency comes with a physically redeemable collector's edition version of the prestige item. Yet, for many, it can be complicated to manage several digital wallets and decentralized goods across platforms. One way to solve this challenge would be creating third parties platforms in the form of crypto banks that would help users deal, trade, and possess NFTs by making transactions frictionless.

description.shortText: Clustered Regularly-Interspaced Short Palindromic Repeats (CRISPR) is a genome-editing technique generated through precise editing of an organism's native genome, even in DIY settings.
description.longTextHtml:
Clustered Regularly-Interspaced Short Palindromic Repeats (CRISPR) is a technique to achieve precise, literal cut-and-paste addition/subtraction of genomes. It relies on two major components: the Cas9 protein that can cut DNA, and the use of a guide RNA, capable of recognizing the sequence of the DNA string that can be edited.

This technology makes it possible to edit genomes by either modifying, deleting, or inserting new sequences to rewrite DNA. The pivotal point involves altering original base pair arrangements within the genome of an organism, without the need to introduce foreign genetic material from another organism.

CRISPR is more agile and accurate than previous or competing models of genetic editing. It opens up a vast range of opportunities that include editing allergens in peanuts, creating mushrooms that do not brown or even breeding genetically-engineered mosquitoes that cannot transmit diseases such as malaria.

By using CRISPR to finely control the activity of specific genes, we can better understand how organic bodies naturally carry out the same process. In terms of human system trials, researchers in China have been looking into editing human cells to create cancer-fighting white blood cells that could be injected into patients or babies vulnerable to HIV. However, despite the infinite possibilities for CRISPR, there are still crucial ethical and moral implications that arise as significant challenges and issues to be discussed, especially regarding the alteration of the human genome. We might have to decide which genes are subject to editing, and which traits are prohibited from being edited in an embryo.

On the other hand, CRISPR CAS9 technology has become a promising alternative for crop improvement. As the world's population is expected to grow substantially in the following decades, maximizing the yield productivity without increasing the environmental impact is one of the many excitement possibilities of CRISPR. Besides, society at large seems more open to CRISPR compared to other techniques like in the case of genetically transformed organisms, also referred to as GMOs, which have experienced intense public backlash.

In addition, it is possible to manipulate a new generation of fish species as a means of creating directional breeding. For example, catfish had its genome sequence 99.7% assessed, making it possible to change their performance traits by manipulating their microRNAs. Some additional features include phenotypic variations to make catfish more resistant to diseases, heat stress, hypoxia, and even reduce their head size.

Future Perspectives

Although CRISPR is currently used in very targeted manners, for example, by developing new model systems or by stimulating the effect of treatments using genetic editing, there is still a lot to be discovered in terms of side-effects and reversibility. Scientists have been looking into the consequences of this gene-editing technique, especially given the fact that it may be impossible to reverse or turn off these edits.

Apart from safety risks, human genome editing poses some massive moral questions. It could offer a chance to edit harmful mutations, but for those living in poverty, genome editing could be used as one more tool for the privileged to vault ahead. Bioethics is currently debating how and where it is mandatory to trace a line within disease treatment and human enhancement to combat the creation of genetic disparities.

Taking this technology one step further, scientists are even considering bringing back extinct species such as the woolly mammoth with the use of the same technology. By following the same concept, companies are testing age-reversal technologies in human clinical trials, the combination of which could extend lifespans by a decade or more. One day it may be possible to eliminate the negative features of aging, erase wrinkles, and potentially wipe out age-related diseases.

attachments.name: Precise Genome Modification via Sequence-Specific Nucleases-Mediated Gene Targeting for Crop Improvement
attachments.description: Genome editing technologies enable precise modifications of DNA sequences in vivo and offer a great promise for harnessing plant genes in crop improvement. The precise manipulation of plant genomes relies on the induction of DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs) by sequence-specific nucleases (SSNs) to initiate DNA repair reactions that are based on either non-homologous end joining (NHEJ) or homology-directed repair (HDR). While complete knock-outs and loss-of-function mutations generated by NHEJ are very valuable in defining gene functions, their applications in crop improvement are somewhat limited because many agriculturally important traits are conferred by random point mutations or indels at specific loci in either the genes’ encoding or promoter regions. Therefore, genome modification through SSNs-mediated HDR for gene targeting (GT) that enables either gene replacement or knock-in will provide an unprecedented ability to facilitate plant breeding by allowing introduction of precise point mutations and new gene functions, or integration of foreign genes at specific and desired ‘safe’ harbor in a predefined manner. The emergence of three programmable SSNs such as zinc finger nucleases (ZFNs), transcriptional activator-like effector nucleases (TALENs), and the clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeat (CRISPR)/CRISPR-associated protein 9 (Cas9) systems has revolutionized genome modification in plants in a more controlled manner. However, while targeted mutagenesis is becoming routine in plants, the potential of GT technology has not been well realized for traits improvement in crops, mainly due to the fact that NHEJ predominates DNA repair process in somatic cells and competes with the HDR pathway, and thus HDR-mediated GT is a relative rare event in plants. Here, we review recent research findings mainly focusing on development and applications of precise GT in plants using three SSNs systems described above, and the potential mechanisms underlying HDR events in plant cells. We then address the challenges and propose future perspectives in order to facilitate the implementation of precise genome modification through SSNs-mediated GT for crop improvement in a global context.

attachments.name: Construction and in vivo assembly of a catalytically proficient and hyperthermostable de novo enzyme
attachments.description: Although catalytic mechanisms in natural enzymes are well understood, achieving the diverse palette of reaction chemistries in re-engineered native proteins has proved challenging. Wholesale modification of natural enzymes is potentially compromised by their intrinsic complexity, which often obscures the underlying principles governing biocatalytic efficiency. The maquette approach can circumvent this complexity by combining a robust de novo designed chassis with a design process that avoids atomistic mimicry of natural proteins. Here, we apply this method to the construction of a highly efficient, promiscuous, and thermostable artificial enzyme that catalyzes a diverse array of substrate oxidations coupled to the reduction of H2O2. The maquette exhibits kinetics that match and even surpass those of certain natural peroxidases, retains its activity at elevated temperature and in the presence of organic solvents, and provides a simple platform for interrogating catalytic intermediates common to natural heme-containing enzymes.

attachments.name: What are genome editing and CRISPR-Cas9?
attachments.description: Genome editing (also called gene editing) is a group of technologies that give scientists the ability to change an organism's DNA. These technologies allow genetic material to be added, removed, or altered at particular locations in the genome. Several approaches to genome editing have been developed. A recent one is known as CRISPR-Cas9, which is short for clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats and CRISPR-associated protein 9. The CRISPR-Cas9 system has generated a lot of excitement in the scientific community because it is faster, cheaper, more accurate, and more efficient than other existing genome editing methods.

attachments.name: Pest control by genetic manipulation of sex ratio.
attachments.description: We model the release of insects carrying an allele at multiple loci that shifts sex ratios in favor of males. We model two approaches to sex ratio alteration. In the first (denoted SD), meiotic segregation (or sperm fertility) is distorted in favor of gametes carrying the male-determining genetic element (e.g., Y-chromosome). It is assumed that any male carrying at least one copy of the SD allele produces only genotypically male offspring. In the second approach (denoted PM), the inserted allele alters sex ratio by causing genetically female individuals to become phenotypically male. It is assumed that any insect carrying at least one copy of the PM allele is phenotypically male. Both approaches reduce future population growth by reducing the number of phenotypic females. The models allow variation in the number of loci used in the release, the size of the release, and the negative fitness effect caused by insertion of each sex ratio altering allele. We show that such releases may be at least 2 orders of magnitude more effective than sterile male releases (SIT) in terms of numbers of surviving insects. For example, a single SD release with two released insects for every wild insect and a 5% fitness cost per inserted allele could reduce the target population to 1/1000th of the no-release population size, whereas a similar-sized SIT release would only reduce the population to one-fifth of its original size. We also compare these two sex ratio alteration approaches to a female-killing (FK) system and the sterile male technique when there are repeated releases over a number of generations. In these comparisons, the SD approach is the most efficient with equivalent pest suppression achieved by release of approximately 1 SD, 1.5-20 PM, 2-70 FK, and 16-3,000 SIT insects, depending on conditions. We also calculate the optimal number of SD and PM allele insertions to be used under various conditions, assuming that there is an additional genetic load incurred for each allelic insertion.

description.shortText: Railway sleepers, made of recycled plastic, able to generate kinetic energy. This railroad material has a longer lifespan, reduced maintenance costs, vibrations, and noise.
description.longTextHtml:
With the same mechanical characteristics as traditional reinforced concrete sleepers, railway energy harvesting can generate and transmit the kinetic energy from the motion produced by trains. Made from recycled plastic, this energy harvesting and storage solution can decrease power consumption, maintenance costs, and increase train services security. Current models have sensors embedded into the platform, used to measure and monitor the performance of the railway system.

Energy can be harvested more efficiently from two different primary sources, such as vibration or solar. Both options are incredibly efficient and clean. One is based on harvesting, recovering, and recycling track vibration. The second one only requires photovoltaic panels to enable renewable energy harvesting. As it made of a recycled by-product, this solution is low-cost and easy to be implemented in current railway infrastructure.

Future Perspectives

Transport represents a high share of greenhouse gas emissions and air pollution. With the global shift towards a low-carbon, circular economy already underway, improving energy efficiency in the sector has become paramount. In the coming years, AI usage in the industry holds massive potential to better understand and improve railway logistics. From traction to infrastructure, all railway elements necessary for trains to operate will work on a zero-emission basis.

attachments.name: Railway vehicle induced vibration energy harvesting and saving of rail transit segmental prefabricated and assembling bridges
attachments.description: Taking a continuous rigid segmental prefabrication and assembly bridge on Guangzhou Metro No.14 as example, railway vehicle induced vibration energy harvesting and saving was studied in this paper. By modeling multi-body dynamics system of B-type railway vehicle and the wheel-rail interaction relationship, train-track-bridge (TTB) response was calculated accurately. Through dynamic analysis of the TTB system with two different track irregularity conditions, vertical acceleration time histories of the track slab were acquired. Based on this, a new type of electromagnetic vibration energy harvesters (EM-VEHs) is proposed. Utilizing the track slab vibration, the EM-VEHs set adjacent to the track slab are demonstrated to be feasible to supply enough power for strain collection units or GPS data transmission units in bridge health monitoring system. Compared with previous research, the power density of the proposed EM-VEH device is much higher. The application prospect of the proposed EM-VEH on urban mass transit SPA bridges is worthy to be anticipated.

attachments.name: Energy harvesting from the vibrations of a passing train: effect of speed variability
attachments.description: This paper builds on a previous study which investigated the amount of energy that could be harvested from the vibration induced by a passing train using a trackside energy harvester. In that study, the optimum parameters of the device were determined for a train passing at a particular speed. However, the effect of the train speed variability on the amount of energy harvested was not explored. In this paper a study is thus undertaken to determine this effect using experimental data from train passages at a site in the UK. Furthermore, a model is developed to investigate the optimum design parameters of the energy harvester when trains pass by at slightly different speeds. This is then validated using the experimental data. It is found that, provided the variability in the train speed is less than about 1% from the nominal speed, then a harvester tuned so that its natural frequency matches one of the trainload dominant frequencies at the line speed is a reasonable design condition.

attachments.description: In order to ensure safety and reliability of railway transportation the interest in monitoring systems is constantly increasing. These devices include sensors and electronic components, which need electric power supply for their proper working. However not all railway lines and vehicles are provided with electric power, furthermore, it can be complex to provide energy to sensors by cables in some location of the vehicle. The demand of a widespread distributed electrical energy can be fulfilled by energy harvesting techniques from primary sources. This paper analyses the different concepts of energy harvesters proposed in literature for the railway field, both for on board and wayside applications. The harvesters are classified according to the source from which energy is harvested and for each type of harvester advantages and disadvantages are critically discussed. The proposed review highlights the most promising solutions regarding energy harvesting in order to support future researches concerning this topic.

description.shortText: Attention could be tokenized in the blockchain distributed ledger to reward users for watch-time or time spent online. The system works by transferring micropayments for each advert seen by a user.
description.longTextHtml:
In the attention economy, the time people spend consuming digital content is perceived and valued as a commodity. Companies, brands, and publishers are thus continuously battling over engagement. Current technologies can measure how much time is spent on a particular website, video, audio, game or application. With blockchain-based platforms, users could be rewarded directly by the advertisers with micropayments in cryptocurrencies, or tokens, for each advert seen, in a consensual manner.

At the moment, this can be done by browsing through unique blockchain-based browsers, which uses the same technology to measure watch-time or time spent. This process cuts the need for a middleman, makes more efficient adverts, guarantees transparency and data safety through a cryptographic ledger, and avoids bot fraud. Tokens acquired might be used to reward online creators for their content, creating a possible new monetization model for this and other kinds of virtual work.

Still, as efficient as it may sound, the process of capitalizing attention is heatedly debated, especially now that this technological solution is gaining popularity. When attention is used as a currency, it is hard to leverage if the digital content seen by the user is something they are in fact, interested in. The act of using adverts that employ psychological strategies to catch the user's attention ensuring they spend more time online than they usually would, remains to be discussed. This should be set at the forefront of the debate, mainly because the field of user experience is profoundly based on this premise. Solutions range from offering the users a wage while engaging online to benefits in digital services.

Future Perspectives

With eye-trackers, it would be possible to measure exactly where users are looking at any given time for a more accurate attention measure. Paired with biometric and brain sensors, emotional responses could also be rewarded. Also, as extended (virtual, mixed or augmented) worlds become more present in our lives, our attention could be measured closely with sensors in our phones, glasses, and other wearables. With these blockchain-based attention tokens, attention key performance indicators such as time-spent and watch time could be rewarded directly to users, disrupting the currently popular advertising-based model of the giant technology platforms.

A climate-controlled agricultural unit, the size of a shipping container, able to grow all sorts of food for small-scale cafeterias, restaurants, or bars. The self-contained farms allow small scale producers to grow a variety of items on-site and offer some of the freshest options possible.

Microculture gardens could be a useful resource for producing a broad range of plant species, including leafy vegetables, fruits, root vegetables, herbs, and more. By shortening the distances between producers and consumers, prices would decrease, as shipping would get significantly cheaper. This farming solution could occupy viable spaces throughout urban communities with small-scale, self-sustaining food forests.

This solution is designed to use less than one meter of space and could be constructed using re-purposed or up-cycled materials. The materials and designs would provide modularity, mobility, and easy replicability. Microculture gardens could also be used to feed isolated groups of people, like maritime crew members or even astronauts, while in missions.

Future Perspectives

Low-income neighborhoods that often lack access to healthy food could benefit by having their communities surrounded by microculture gardens that provide fresh produce throughout the year. By letting communities manage their micro-gardens autonomously, they could not only offer self-sufficiency but also an income source as cultivated food could be sold.

archive.name: Voiceless Speech Interface

description.shortText: An interface that transmits messages without generating audible sounds by picking up on nerve signals sent to the vocal cords, analyzing and translating them into messages that can be delivered to other recipients.
description.longTextHtml:
When words are silently “said” inside the head (a process called subvocalization), the brain triggers microscopic reactions in the muscled used to produce speech. Since the myoelectric signals emitted by these muscles are highly individual to each person, it is very difficult to detect and interpret them for the recognition of the words spoken internally.

Powered with a machine learning system base on an artificial neural network that needs to be re-trained for each user, electrodes contained in wearables would detect neuromuscular signals and recognize what the user has “said”. The muscular activity in the jaw and face would transmit internal verbalizations, undetectable to the human eye, and this device would interpret the subvocal signals to identify which words the user had in mind.

Once trained, this technological solution has a variety of applications. Looking up information on a smartphone during conversations requires shifting one's attention from the conversation to the handheld device, for instance. By using a voiceless speech interface, these interactions could be drastically simplified, allowing the user to interact with their personal assistant by silently voicing commands without having to leave the context of the original conversation.

Furthermore, it could allow voice communication in high-noise environments, such as the flight deck of an aircraft carrier, in power plants, near printing presses, or at other loud manufacturing facilities. Conversely, in silent settings or places with possible eavesdroppers such as during a military operation, voiceless communication could replace forms of silent communication such as hand gestures. In healthcare, speech could be restored to people unable to vocalize. In extended reality, these sensors could give a voice to virtual avatars of people with speaking disabilities.

Future Perspectives

The added convenience of this technology also comes with a substantial risk of intrusiveness. Is it vital to have electrodes reading human thoughts while grocery shopping? Invasion of privacy could become a concern and require a whole new set of policies designed to protect mental secrecy.

The implementation of such a system could be an important step towards achieving a transhuman body with seamless interaction with the Internet. It would be a step towards a more general brain-computer interface.

description.shortText: AI software that supports legal prosecutions by automatically detecting and enforcing sentences. The Internet of Things would feed nearly unhackable data into the system to ensure informed decision-making while addressing law-breaking.
description.longTextHtml:
AI software that supports legal prosecution by automatically detecting and enforcing sentences, using historical data and harm assessment algorithms to analyze criminal databases. This software is fed with data derived from CCTV cameras and surveillance biometric recognition systems. The data is then turned into evidence, thus helping provide educational insights, enforce penalties for convicted criminals, or issue automatic fines and tickets. The algorithms could also be trained to give offenders a score to categorize the severity of their unlawful act.

Different studies have proven that the information gathered by those devices could be used for criminal assessment, and function as a significant deterrent for bad behavior. The resulting predictions from these algorithms could help in pretrial, parole, and sentencing decisions. As automation takes over the judiciary and police systems, resources could be used more efficiently while saving capital.

Private institutions could also use this technological solution by accessing and editing a cloud-based database. Establishments could share real-time CCTV camera content with the cloud for the system to analyze and send instant alerts whenever an intruder enters the establishment. The user can also alert the community at large when a crime occurs, adding images of the suspect(s) to watchlists and criminal databases.

However, this type of AI usage is subject to criticism because it could be used to reinforce societal biases. Solutions created to avoid algorithmic prejudices range from eliminating offensive and prejudicial content — usually designed under white-male perspectives — from algorithmic structures, to hiring a diverse team of developers consisting of minority groups.

Future Perspectives

As judiciary systems around the world begin to see the potential of connected devices and artificial intelligence, surveillance and the usage of algorithms may become mandatory to keep the peace and keep criminals off the streets. Although the debate on issues of privacy, reinforcing bias and stereotypes continues, these subjects may be harder to justify, given the myriad of evidence and peace of mind that this technology could achieve. In the case of a private shared database, any user could be able to add a subject to the "criminal" list, thus creating a scenario of peer-based vigilance, in which every citizen is a node in a surveillance state.

These predictions are used in pretrial, parole, and sentencing decisions. Proponents of these systems argue that big data and advanced machine learning make these analyses more accurate and less biased than humans. We show, however, that the widely used commercial risk assessment software COMPAS is no more accurate or fair than predictions made by people with little or no criminal justice expertise. In addition, despite COMPAS’s collection of 137 features, the same accuracy can be achieved with a simple linear classifier with only two features.

archive.name: Blockchain Prediction Market

description.shortText: A protocol that uses the power of crowd data to forecast and predict events by allowing the buying and selling of shares in a specific outcome.
description.longTextHtml:
A speculative market where participants trade information. Investors, in this environment, bet on the outcomes of future events. Smart investors will do their research, experts will weigh in, and insiders on the subject will bet on the most likely outcome. Thus, prediction markets serve as aggregators of information.

The model works on the principle that the wisdom of the crowds will always be superior to the data known to only a few experts. As opinions are tokenized or used as stakes, they require more foundation, thus creating a more rational logic than mere beliefs or feelings. By financially incentivizing individuals to share their knowledge on the market, more deliberate insights into social, industrial, and political trends can be generated.

Today, most prediction market platforms are centralized and have limitations, including local regulations, owners’ reluctance to list specific contracts, trust in the operator of the platform, and the payment of additional fees for the ability to make use of their services. By replacing this process with a decentralized or distributed blockchain-based solution, many benefits are delivered, such as censorship-resistance, a reduced number of intermediaries, and increased accessibility.

A decentralized prediction market is harder to shut down, either by governments or malicious actors. On blockchain, every node on the network runs the code, and smart contracts are built to a certain standard. No user would be able to edit or delete the programs that underpin the market. Also, blockchain doesn’t require administrators or intermediaries and is outsourced to automated codes, meaning that they don’t pay fees to a third party.

In order to determine which outcome has occurred at the time of expiry, a truth mechanism is put in place. Since the blockchain and smart contracts cannot access off-chain data, such as if the outcome happened or not, the concept of blockchain oracle was introduced. They are third-party services that serve as bridges between blockchains and the outside world. A blockchain oracle could be linked to a third-party website or feed, however misinformation or media manipulation could undermine the essence of the blockchain. Another option is to financially incentivize users to truthfully report on events, by implementing staking mechanisms, which require users to put forward tokens to become reporters in that dynamic. If they report correctly, they are rewarded, if not, they will lose their stake. The decentralization of this concept enhances its potential as a prediction tool. Also, as more capable oracles are advanced, blockchain technology could host provably fair code that cannot be tampered with.

Future Perspectives

Before the launch of the blockchain, economist Robin Hanson suggested a democratic model based on prediction markets known as Futarchy. He claimed this could be a democratic tool in which elected officials could define measures of national wellbeing to determine which policies would have the most positive effect. If implemented in the blockchain, this could bring a new narrative to democracy, with more participation from the people. However, some issues we face today might still occur in this model, such as media manipulation, lobbying, and majoritarian democracy. Still, Blockchain Prediction Markets could have a significant influence on trends forecast across different markets, as it excels at amassing and representing information in a decentralized and trustless manner.

description.shortText: Aquatic uncrewed vehicles designed to clean up waste and pollution as well as logging real-time water quality data. They float on the surface of the water, scooping up litter, biomass, microplastics, and other detritus.
description.longTextHtml:
Drones equipped with a floating structure used in aquatic settings for monitoring, collecting real-time water quality data, and cleaning up waste and pollution in water bodies. These uncrewed vehicles are equipped with LiDAR to avoid collisions from up to 60 meters away, along with IoT sensors for measuring factors such as temperature, pH, depth, and green algae. Also, together with GPS waypoints and autonomous software, aquatic drones can follow set pathways, which can be selected according to currents and tide pools, floating on the water's surface, scooping up litter, biomass, microplastics, and other detritus.

Current models resemble a small catamaran with a sieve-like basket underneath and are powered by a lithium-ion battery that can last up to 10 hours. The drones’ capacity for autonomous operation is improving, as the vehicle is still human-supervised. Velocity and steering are preprogrammed and performed autonomously by the drone, but whenever abnormal circumstances occur, operators are required to control the vehicle. Currently, aquatic drones are used in urban settings and more stable waterbodies or slow-moving currents such as canals, ports, rivers, and lakes.

Future Perspectives

With 5G and more powerful computing capacity, aquatic drones could be grouped to swarm, collect water-quality data, and maritime life information in a holistic approach. They could also be used around off-shore platforms to supervise activities around the premises and warn the operation centers when incidents take place. In the future, they could also be solar-powered or propelled by organic batteries, thus avoiding any toxic waste to spill into the water.

Moreover, with the evolution of the integrated sensing technology, in the future, aquatic drones will be capable of real-time recognizing micro-concentrations of specific chemicals, such as algae toxins, and identify their source based on the diffusion pattern of these chemicals in the water, potentially allowing the exploration of novel substances for the pharmaceutical and the cosmetics industries.

attachments.name: Mapping water quality using aquatic drones
attachments.description: NEWS - April 2020 Robbert de Lange is an MSc student Water Management, and was in Myanmar from February until April to measure the lake quality at different locations using a drone. He did this project in cooperation with INDYMO. INDYMO is a Dutch start-up that works in the field of the management of water resources and water quality. INDYMO focuses on innovative ways of monitoring water quality and ecology using underwater and water surface drones (dynamic monitoring) equipped with water quality sensors (e.g. dissolved oxygen, electrical conductivity, chlorophyll, blue-green algae), sonar and video cameras. The mobility of sensors and cameras provide a low-cost and rapid 3D assessment of surface water quality with high spatial resolution and quality. Water drones have already been tested in Indonesia, Vietnam, Mali and Peru, and are now being used for assessing the condition of water resources in Myanmar.

attachments.name: Multivariate sensor signals collected by aquatic drones involved in water monitoring: A complete dataset - ScienceDirect
attachments.description: Sensor data generated by intelligent systems, such as autonomous robots, smart buildings and other systems based on artificial intelligence, represent valuable sources of knowledge in today's data-driven society, since they contain information about the situations these systems face during their operation. These data are usually multivariate time series since modern technologies enable the simultaneous acquisition of multiple signals during long periods of time. In this paper we present a dataset containing sensor traces of six data acquisition campaigns performed by autonomous aquatic drones involved in water monitoring. A total of 5.6 h of navigation are available, with data coming from both lakes and rivers, and from different locations in Italy and Spain. The monitored variables concern both the internal state of the drone (e.g., battery voltage, GPS position and signals to propellers) and the state of the water (e.g., temperature, dissolved oxygen and electrical conductivity). Data were collected in the context of the EU-funded Horizon 2020 project INTCATCH (http://www.intcatch.eu) which aims to develop a new paradigm for monitoring water quality of catchments. The aquatic drones used for data acquisition are Platypus Lutra boats. Both autonomous and manual drive is used in different parts of the navigation. The dataset is analyzed in the paper “Time series segmentation for state-model generation of autonomous aquatic drones: A systematic framework” [1] by means of recent time series clustering/segmentation techniques to extract data-driven models of the situations faced by the drones in the data acquisition campaigns. These data have strong potential for reuse in other kinds of data analysis and evaluation of machine learning methods on real-world datasets [2]. Moreover, we consider this dataset valuable also for the variety of situations faced by the drone, from which machine learning techniques can learn behavioral patterns or detect anomalous activities. We also provide manual labeling for some known states of the drones, such as, drone inside/outside the water, upstream/downstream navigation, manual/autonomous drive, and drone turning, that represent a ground truth for validation purposes. Finally, the real-world nature of the dataset makes it more challenging for machine learning methods because it contains noisy samples collected while the drone was exposed to atmospheric agents and uncertain water flow conditions.

description.shortText: A driverless vehicle, fully automated in all conditions. It has no steering wheels and pedals and does not require any human control to operate.
description.longTextHtml:
A vehicle that does not require any human control to operate. It could take a passenger to any chosen destination by itself. Embedded with different sensors and connected to an integrated digital system, it would monitor and maneuver through all types of road conditions. Unlike the highly automated self-driving vehicle, it would not be restricted to geo-fenced locations, thus eliminating the need for a steering wheel and pedals. Regarding exceptional situations, this vehicle would have a series of emergency features and safety protocols, being able to communicate with the other riders using vehicle-vehicle communication software.

This type of vehicle, considered level five of automation, is currently being used, at a trial phase, in situations such as robotic taxis service. For these vehicles to move into mass production and adoption, it would be necessary to have a legislative structure, which is yet to be addressed. Self-driving vehicles might be a very efficient application of AI technology. However, they still face significant challenges: the unpredictable behavior of humans, for instance, could convert these cars into a threat to people. Although most of the technological capacity is already available to project an artificially intelligent vehicle and many prototypes are being manufactured, due to the regulations regarding safety, these cars might still be years away from being implemented.

Future Perspectives

With the existence of fully automated vehicles, driver's licenses would no longer be part of our world. Therefore, it would enable many people who are not capable of driving to have the chance to become more independent as they move around the city. Also, some types of workers and professionals would have their time spared to undertake work-related activities while commuting, such as having quick meetings or catching up with emails and messages.

Besides that, the implementation of fully autonomous cars could as well make roads safer and mitigate the traffic. Parking spaces, from houses with garages to whole buildings that today are projected to be parking lots, would no longer be necessary. Driverless cars could as well play a significant role in architectural shifts in the urban environment, such as eliminating the need to have a personal car, thus directly influencing a city's traffic.

archive.name: Autonomous Agriculture Vehicle

description.shortText: AI developments embedded in agricultural vehicles such as tractors designed to take over horticultural tasks such as pruning, weeding, spraying, harvesting, tilling, and monitoring.
description.longTextHtml:
An autonomous self-propelled vehicle, managed by a combination of video cameras, radar, accelerometers, a LIDAR system, and onboard software, which perform agricultural activities and transportation without the need for a driver. By eliminating the need to have someone at the wheel, this technology drastically reduces the time and cost of production and transportation. Agricultural vehicles operate in a significantly safer environment than conventional road systems. They could, therefore, see quicker adoption and serve as a stepping stone to fully autonomous self-driving vehicles across the board.

Most robots used in agriculture are designed to replace human labor at the harvesting stage, such as fruit-picking robots, driverless tractors, or milkbots. So far, proper execution of tasks has been difficult because of the specificity and peculiarities of trade, including the size and color of the fruit to be picked. However, AI developments may eventually facilitate the creation of self-learning robots that can take over other horticultural tasks such as pruning, weeding, spraying, and monitoring.

These features would open up access to machinery control and the data gateway while contributing to farming autonomy by showing the tractor’s progress in the field and giving farmers the possibility of simultaneously and remotely managing many different crops off-site. For ground transportation, independent trucks would no longer be hindered by the needs and limits of human drivers.

Future Perspectives

Since there is no need for an operator on board, autonomous vehicles could operate 24 hours a day without stopping. Besides, further developments to reduce their size and radically redesign their shape would result in significant changes. The smaller size and possibly slower speeds due to longer operating hours could introduce higher levels of precision, and higher specialization of vehicles. The same idea would apply not only to farming itself but also as a means to automate the logistics sector without the need for drivers.

However, as the trend of using autonomous machines to supply our needs is continually growing, the concern over maintaining human labor in agriculture rises as well. For a future in which devices are supporting our activities, we must also take care of the unprivileged sectors of society, which will be at risk of losing their jobs. Accordingly, to avoid facing an employment crisis, it would be interesting to take a look at educational strategies to provide knowledge about autonomous devices. Regulatory frameworks will be needed to tackle potential implications of digital agricultural technologies for farm labor and rural communities in the future since automated equipment could transform the farming workforce as we know it today.

Through careful planning, this digital shift can positively contribute to growth in rural communities by creating new work opportunities. Farmers will redeploy their employees to value-added tasks and new tasks to control and program autonomous machines. This more transparent manner could help ease the continually evolving process of human relationships with robots and AI, thus making the transition less of a challenge.

archive.name: Sociometric Badge

description.shortText: A type of identification in the form of a wearable, microchip implant, or AR badge that gathers personal data from locations, social media profiles, and interactions of individuals. It analyzes the data and provides feedback regarding activities, emotions, conversations, and published content.
description.longTextHtml:
A type of identification that could take the form of a wearable, microchip implant, or AR badge, it can gather personal data from locations and interactions of individuals. This information can be analyzed to give feedback regarding activities, emotions, conversations, and published content. AR badges can go a step further, in which fiduciary markers can display the desired information through AR glasses or even eye-projectors.

During human interactions, individuals express —and often hide— several emotions, feelings, and thoughts. Social relationships can be overwhelming for some, and sociometric badges are designed to ease this process. This technological solution records geolocation, oral conversations, and data from social media, and then captures and measures what exactly happens between individuals, such as how each individual felt by analyzing the pitch of their voice.

In order to address solutions to understand sociological behavior, governments and organizations may use these badges to monitor individuals according to their needs or constitutions. It would facilitate the process of law comprehension and acceptance. In educational environments, these badges enable teachers to take their students outside structured environments like classrooms while maintaining the ability to measure their level of engagement and provide personalized feedback objectively.

Types of use can multiply when considering the many activities that happen inside of schools. Some examples include using the device to analyze the effectiveness of peer learning (e.g., analyzing geo-locations for interaction patterns and creating social networks of who-learns-with-whom) or even to uncover school bullies by analyzing voice pitches to detect 'anger' or 'fear.'

Even if promising, sociometric badges raise considerable concerns regarding privacy. Although the sensitive information gathered in these devices is intended to be shared among other individuals, the act of continuously carrying an identification that displays private data brings up fundamental questions whether this technology is used to help in social relationships or to control human behavior.

Future Perspectives

Although an individual could wear these badges, this type of tracking device may be anywhere and everywhere as connectivity grows, and the price of microchips drops. Also, biological information could be used to enrich the gathered data and, therefore, give more precise information about users.

As extended reality flourishes, they could also be used as an additional digital layer to social life, displaying clout, status, and personality traits depending on what the user wants the world to see. A person might choose to display their marital status, a horoscope sign, badges earned in games or sports, the team they support, or the company they work for.

attachments.name: Sociometric Badges
attachments.description: A sociometric badge (commonly known as a "sociometer") is a wearable electronic device capable of automatically measuring the amount of face-to-face  interaction, conversational time, physical proximity to other people, and physical activity levels using social signals derived from vocal features, body motion, and relative location. We have built several hundred sociometric badges and used them in real organizations to automatically measure individual and collective patterns of behavior, predict human behavior from unconscious social signals, identify social affinity among individuals working in the same team, and enhance social interactions by providing feedback to the users of our system.
